ground_truth.description: PriceAware.getCurrentPriceInPeg() allows callers to request a current-block price. When forceCurBlock is true and the update window has elapsed, the function obtains a Uniswap-style AMM quote and can update the cached token price from that quote. Because the quote is computed from current pair reserves, a flash loan can temporarily distort the reserves and cause the protocol to use a manipulated price.
ground_truth.impact: Wrong prices break the core functionality of the contracts such as borrowing on margin, liquidations, etc.
ground_truth.mitigation: Do not use the current Uniswap spot quote as the token price. Use a TWAP oracle based on Uniswap cumulative price variables.
ground_truth.title: [H-03] Price feed can be manipulated

predictions.description: Liquidation eligibility and liquidation valuation rely on current Uniswap-style AMM reserves rather than a manipulation-resistant price. CrossMarginAccounts.belowMaintenanceThreshold and IsolatedMarginAccounts.belowMaintenanceThreshold call getCurrentPriceInPeg with forceCurBlock set to true. In that mode, PriceAware.getCurrentPriceInPeg either returns getPriceFromAMM or viewCurrentPriceInPeg, both of which derive prices using UniswapStyleLib.getAmountsOut and current pair reserves. An attacker can temporarily manipulate the configured AMM path, then call the public liquidation function while collateral is undervalued or debt is overvalued. The account may be incorrectly classified as liquidatable and permanently deleted. The same AMM paths are also used for liquidation execution, and the liquidation swaps use effectively unrestricted slippage parameters.
predictions.impact: Healthy cross-margin or isolated-margin accounts may be liquidated, collateral may be sold at manipulated prices, residual user payouts may be reduced or eliminated, and the protocol may incur liquidation shortfalls or lender haircuts. Maintainer and attacker compensation can also be calculated from distorted liquidation results.
predictions.mitigation: Use a manipulation-resistant oracle, such as a sufficiently long TWAP, an independent oracle, or a validated multi-source price, for liquidation eligibility and account valuation. Do not return a current AMM spot quote when forceCurBlock is true. Separate price updates from liquidation decisions and require a previously finalized, fresh price with maximum-deviation and stale-price checks. Add oracle-based minimum-output or maximum-input bounds to liquidation swaps instead of using amountOutMin equal to zero or amountInMax equal to type(uint256).max. Consider limiting liquidation batch size or using an auction for large positions.
predictions.title: AMM spot-price manipulation can trigger wrongful margin liquidations

predictions.description: CrossMarginAccounts.positiveBalance authorizes borrowing and withdrawals by comparing holdings and debt valued through PriceAware.getCurrentPriceInPeg with forceCurBlock set to false. When a price is uninitialized, the function directly returns an AMM-derived quote. When the cached price is stale, it refreshes the cache using getPriceFromAMM, which reads current AMM reserves. The EMA-style update weight and update window limit individual movements but do not make the underlying spot-price observation manipulation-resistant. An attacker can overvalue collateral or undervalue debt, then invoke crossBorrow, crossOvercollateralizedBorrow, or crossWithdraw while the favorable valuation is used.
predictions.impact: An attacker may borrow or withdraw more value than their collateral supports, leaving an undercollateralized account and potential bad debt for lenders, liquidity providers, or the protocol. The cooling-off period does not prevent manipulation by an existing account after the period has elapsed.
predictions.mitigation: Use an independent, manipulation-resistant oracle for collateral and debt valuation. Require prices to be initialized and sufficiently fresh before permitting borrowing or withdrawal; do not fall back to a current AMM quote for an uninitialized asset. Separate oracle updates from user borrowing and withdrawal transactions, use fixed-notional or normalized observations, and enforce maximum-deviation, liquidity, and stale-price checks. Value collateral conservatively and debt at a conservative higher price where multiple observations are available.
predictions.title: AMM-derived valuations can bypass cross-margin borrowing and withdrawal collateral checks

predictions.description: IsolatedMarginAccounts.positiveBalance determines whether additional debt can be recorded using holdingInPeg and loanInPeg, both of which call PriceAware.getCurrentPriceInPeg with forceCurBlock set to false. For an uninitialized or stale price, PriceAware obtains or refreshes the value from current AMM reserves through getPriceFromAMM and UniswapStyleLib.getAmountsOut. An attacker able to manipulate the configured AMM can make the holding token appear more valuable or the borrow token appear cheaper when the isolated borrowing flow reaches borrow and positiveBalance.
predictions.impact: If the authorized isolated-margin trading route can be reached during the manipulated price state, an attacker may create debt that is not adequately backed by collateral. After the AMM price normalizes, the position may become undercollateralized, causing bad debt, liquidation losses, or lender haircuts.
predictions.mitigation: Use a manipulation-resistant and independently validated oracle for isolated-margin collateral checks. Require explicit oracle initialization, freshness, sufficient market liquidity, and bounded deviation before allowing borrowing. Do not update the oracle from a spot AMM quote during the same transaction that authorizes borrowing; instead consume a previously finalized price snapshot and apply conservative collateral and debt valuations.
predictions.title: AMM-derived prices can permit undercollateralized isolated-margin borrowing

ground_truth.description: Synth.realise() calculates baseValueLP with Utils.calcLiquidityHoldings() from the pool's current baseAmount/tokenAmount reserves and total LP supply, and calculates baseValueSynth with Utils.calcActualSynthUnits() using the same current reserve ratio. If the manipulated values make the LP holdings appear to exceed the synth value, realise() treats the difference as a premium and burns LP tokens from the pool. A flash loan or a large LP holder can shift the AMM ratio before calling realise(), then shift it back and repeat the operation.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can use transient AMM-ratio manipulation to cause LP tokens held by Synth to be burned, then redeem their own LP tokens for a larger share of the pool's underlying assets, extracting value from other pool LP holders.
ground_truth.mitigation: Do not value LP tokens with the instantaneous AMM spot price. Use a manipulation-resistant TWAP or Chainlink oracle for token pricing, or use an anti-flash-loan LP valuation formula such as Alpha Finance's fair-LP formula.
ground_truth.title: [H-05] Synth realise is vulnerable to flash loan attacks

ground_truth.description: SynthVault._deposit() converts the deposited synth amount into BASE weight using Utils.calcSpotValueInBase(), which ultimately computes amount * pool.baseAmount() / pool.tokenAmount() from current AMM reserves. The resulting weight is stored and later used by calcReward() to allocate an unrelated BASE reward reserve. An attacker can temporarily increase the BASE-per-token spot price, deposit synth while the price is distorted, and then restore the pool; the inflated stored weight remains after the manipulation ends.
ground_truth.impact: The attacker can inflate their stored SynthVault weight relative to the deposited synth amount and claim a large share of BASE-funded rewards. The cost of manipulation depends on pool liquidity and the potential profit depends on the reward reserve, so the attack can be profitable under certain circumstances.
ground_truth.mitigation: Track a TWAP price of the synth, store deposited synth amounts, and calculate user and total weight on the fly from the TWAP multiplied by the deposit amount instead of at deposit time.
ground_truth.title: [H-06] SynthVault rewards can be gamed

ground_truth.description: DAO.bond() calls handleTransferIn(), which calculates the BASE allocation for a bonded token amount through Utils.calcSwapValueInBase() using the pool's current reserves before adding the token and BASE as liquidity for BondVault. Because the reserve-dependent swap calculation can be changed by manipulating the pool, an attacker can distort the allocation, repeatedly trigger bonding, and then reverse the manipulation.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can cause the DAO's Bond allocation to be stolen by making the DAO commit BASE at manipulated exchange rates and then recovering a disproportionate share of the BASE supplied to the pool.
ground_truth.mitigation: Track a TWAP spot price for the TOKEN/BASE pair and verify that the BASE incentive is within an acceptable range of the TWAP before the DAO commits BASE at the manipulated price.
ground_truth.title: [M-14] BondVault `BASE` incentive can be gamed

predictions.description: Utils.calcSpotValueInBaseWithPool derives token value from the instantaneous pool reserve ratio, baseAmount / tokenAmount. These reserves can be changed through permissionless swaps and public synchronization. SynthVault._deposit uses this value to permanently increase mapMemberSynth_weight, mapMemberTotal_weight, and totalWeight. An attacker can manipulate the relevant pool price, deposit synth tokens while the distorted price is active, and retain an inflated reward weight after the pool price is restored. The stored weight is subsequently used by SynthVault.calcReward and harvestSingle to determine the attacker’s share of Reserve-funded rewards.
predictions.impact: An attacker may receive a disproportionate share of Reserve-funded incentives, diluting rewards owed to honest SynthVault depositors and potentially causing excessive BASE to be converted into synth rewards for the attacker. The accounting distortion persists after the temporary pool-price manipulation ends.
predictions.mitigation: Use a manipulation-resistant valuation source, such as a sufficiently long TWAP or an independent oracle with freshness and deviation checks, when assigning SynthVault weight. Do not make a permanent reward entitlement from a single transaction-time spot price. Consider applying a pricing delay, time-weighted balances, minimum liquidity requirements, and maximum permitted price deviations before a deposit becomes reward-eligible.
predictions.title: Manipulable spot price permanently inflates SynthVault reward weight

predictions.description: Dao.handleTransferIn calculates the protocol-funded SPARTA amount for a bond using Utils.calcSwapValueInBase. That function uses the current Pool.baseAmount and Pool.tokenAmount through calcSwapValueInBaseWithPool and calcSwapOutput. The reserves can be altered by permissionless pool swaps immediately before Dao.bond is called. The calculated SPARTA allocation is then supplied alongside the user’s asset through Router.addLiquidityForMember, and the resulting LP units are minted to the BondVault and credited to the bonding user. No TWAP, independent oracle, deviation bound, maximum allocation, or minimum LP-output check protects this valuation.
predictions.impact: A manipulated price can cause the protocol to contribute an incorrect amount of SPARTA for a bonded asset and issue an incorrect number of LP units. If the inflated allocation exceeds the cost of manipulating and restoring the pool price, the attacker can obtain an oversized LP claim, diluting existing liquidity providers or imposing a loss on protocol-controlled funds.
predictions.mitigation: Value bonded assets using a TWAP, independent oracle, or another manipulation-resistant reference price rather than the instantaneous reserves of the destination pool. Add pool-liquidity and bond-size limits, compare the quote against a reference price with deviation checks, and enforce a maximum SPARTA allocation and an expected LP-unit range before completing the bond.
predictions.title: Manipulable pool reserves control bond LP allocation

predictions.description: Pool.sync is externally callable by any account and sets baseAmount and tokenAmount directly to the pool’s raw token balances. An attacker can transfer BASE or the pool token directly to a pool and call sync, causing the unsolicited balance to become authoritative reserve data. These reserves are then used by Utils spot and swap valuation functions, SynthVault deposits, bond valuation, synth calculations, and pool operations. Pool helper functions also derive pending inputs from the difference between raw balances and recorded reserves, so arbitrary balance changes can be interpreted inconsistently as either liquidity input or pricing reserve.
predictions.impact: The attacker can distort the pool’s effective price and any subsequent calculation that relies on the synchronized reserves. This can produce incorrect reward weights, bonding allocations, synthetic valuations, and swap outcomes. The exact profitability depends on pool liquidity, available incentives, and the cost of the donated assets, but the source establishes a concrete attacker-controlled path to security-sensitive reserve manipulation.
predictions.mitigation: Do not allow arbitrary raw balances to redefine reserves used for pricing and reward accounting. Restrict synchronization to validated protocol flows or maintain separate accounting reserves updated only by authorized swaps, liquidity operations, and protocol distributions. Treat unsolicited transfers as donations or pending balances that cannot immediately affect price-sensitive operations. Add reserve-deviation and delayed-activation checks before synchronized values are used for financial calculations.
predictions.title: Permissionless sync converts unsolicited token transfers into pricing reserves

predictions.description: Utils.calcActualSynthUnits values outstanding synth debt using the instantaneous ratio of Pool.baseAmount to Pool.tokenAmount. Public pool swaps can change this ratio immediately before Synth.realise is called. Synth.realise compares the manipulated synth value with the value of LP collateral and, when the LP value is higher, calculates a premium and burns corresponding LP units held by the synth contract. The calculation has no TWAP, historical observation, independent oracle, price-deviation check, or cap on collateral burned per realization.
predictions.impact: A manipulated reserve ratio can cause Synth.realise to burn an excessive amount of LP collateral, reducing collateral backing outstanding synth debt. Remaining LP holders may receive a larger proportional claim after synth-held LP units are burned, and synth positions may become undercollateralized.
predictions.mitigation: Use a manipulation-resistant price, such as a TWAP or independently validated oracle, for synth-debt valuation. Add minimum liquidity and maximum price-deviation checks, impose a cooldown or delayed price observation for realization, and cap the amount of LP collateral that can be burned in a single realization. Also validate that the supplied pool corresponds to the synth’s LayerONE asset before performing collateral calculations.
predictions.title: Spot-price manipulation can trigger excessive synth collateral burning

predictions.description: Utils.getPoolShareWeight calculates weight as LP units multiplied by Pool.baseAmount divided by LP totalSupply. Pool.baseAmount is mutable through public swaps and Pool.sync. BondVault and DaoVault store the resulting weight when positions are deposited or updated, while existing users’ weights are not automatically recalculated when the pool reserve changes. An attacker can manipulate the pool state before triggering a weight recalculation through a bond, deposit, or claim-related operation, causing the newly stored weight to be inconsistent with other participants’ historical weights. The stored weight affects DAO reward allocation and combined governance voting weight.
predictions.impact: The attacker may obtain an excessive share of reserve-funded DAO rewards, dilute rewards of honest users, and distort governance voting power. The impact depends on pool liquidity, the size of the manipulated reserve change, available reserve incentives, and whether the attacker can economically benefit from the resulting weight.
predictions.mitigation: Do not derive persistent reward or governance weight from an instantaneous mutable pool reserve. Use a TWAP, delayed valuation snapshot, independently validated price, or a valuation index updated under controlled conditions. Ensure all positions use a common valuation epoch, and apply minimum liquidity, deviation, and cooldown checks before a changed pool valuation can affect rewards or voting power.
predictions.title: Mutable pool valuation controls stored DAO and bond reward weight

ground_truth.description: AssetHandler.getLiquidityTokenValue() loads the current market and values a liquidity token from its proportional asset-cash and fCash claims. getCashClaims() and getHaircutCashClaims() derive those claims from mutable totalAssetCash and totalfCash reserves relative to totalLiquidity, while the fCash component is discounted using the lagged oracleRate. A flash-loan-funded lend or borrow can atomically change the reserve composition. Although this manipulation only increases the token's unadjusted value, the risk-adjusted collateral value can fall because the fCash claim receives an additional fCash haircut while the asset-cash claim does not.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can temporarily reduce a direct liquidity provider's risk-adjusted collateral value and cause an account near minimum collateralization to appear undercollateralized and become eligible for liquidation.
ground_truth.mitigation: Do not use current market reserves to determine liquidity-token collateral value. Use a manipulation-resistant TWAP to determine the liquidity token's collateral value.
ground_truth.title: [H-10] Liquidity token value can be manipulated

ground_truth.description: Borrowing a large amount of an asset changes the market's lastImpliedRate. Because the rate oracle is updated with a lagged time window, the manipulated rate can be used during fCash valuation before the oracle fully reflects the prior market state. The resulting risk-adjusted present value can decrease even though the underlying borrowing action is otherwise permitted.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can make an account near the minimum collateralization threshold appear undercollateralized and force its liquidation by temporarily moving the market rate through a large borrow.
ground_truth.mitigation: Increase the rate oracle's time window so that a short-lived rate change caused by a large borrow has less immediate influence on fCash valuation and liquidation eligibility.
ground_truth.title: [M-07] Attackers can force liquidations by borrowing large amounts of an asset.

predictions.description: The nToken redemption path can sell fCash through the current AMM state without enforcing a minimum output, maximum execution rate, oracle-deviation bound, or caller-supplied slippage parameter. In `nTokenRedeemAction._sellfCashAssets`, fCash received from redeemed liquidity-token positions is exchanged using `Market.calculateTrade`. That function derives execution pricing from mutable market reserves and implied-rate state, rather than `market.oracleRate`, and the redemption accepts any nonzero result. An attacker can temporarily move the relevant market through a large lend or borrow before a redemption executes, causing the redeemer's fCash to be sold at an unfavorable price. The attacker may subsequently reverse the market position, subject to liquidity and trading costs.
predictions.impact: NToken redeemers may receive materially less asset cash than expected. The loss is borne by the redeemer and may become significant for large redemptions or markets with limited liquidity. Integrators cannot protect users with a redemption-specific minimum-output parameter because the affected redemption entry point does not expose one.
predictions.mitigation: Add a caller-provided minimum aggregate asset-cash output, or equivalent maximum execution-price and price-impact bounds, to `nTokenRedeem`. Enforce the bound after `_sellfCashAssets` completes and before crediting the redeemer. Consider adding an oracle-deviation check as an additional safeguard, while preserving the distinction between execution pricing and valuation pricing.
predictions.title: NToken redemption lacks execution-price slippage protection

predictions.description: Permissionless trades can immediately modify `market.totalfCash` and `market.totalAssetCash` through `Market.calculateTrade`. These current reserve values are then used by `AssetHandler.getLiquidityTokenValue`, `AssetHandler.getCashClaims`, and `AssetHandler.getHaircutCashClaims` to determine the cash and fCash claims of liquidity tokens. The resulting fCash claim is discounted using the lagged `oracleRate`, but the underlying reserve composition remains based on the immediately mutable market state. Consequently, a trader can temporarily alter the cash/fCash composition used in free-collateral, liquidation, and nToken present-value calculations without the corresponding composition being smoothed by the oracle. The same valuation is used by nToken minting through `nTokenHandler.getNTokenAssetPV`, so a temporary reserve imbalance can also distort the nToken mint exchange ratio and market-deployment decision.
predictions.impact: Temporary market manipulation may cause liquidity-token and nToken collateral to be overvalued or undervalued, affecting free-collateral results, liquidation eligibility, liquidation quantities, and collateral transferred to liquidators. NToken minting may issue an incorrect number of tokens for a deposit or choose an unintended lending-versus-liquidity path. The resulting value transfer depends on market depth, oracle-window duration, exposed collateral, and the attacker's ability to execute and unwind the market trades.
predictions.mitigation: Use a valuation method that is internally consistent with the protected oracle rate. For collateral, liquidation, and nToken valuation, derive liquidity-token cash/fCash claims from time-weighted or historical reserve snapshots, an oracle-consistent virtual-reserve model, or a conservative lower-bound methodology rather than the immediately current `totalfCash` and `totalAssetCash`. Consider delaying collateral-sensitive operations after material market changes, applying additional conservative haircuts, and adding a user-controlled `minTokensToMint` bound for nToken minting.
predictions.title: Spot market reserve composition can manipulate liquidity-token and nToken valuation

ground_truth.description: AuctionEscapeHatch._calculateMaltRequiredForExit() obtains Malt's current market price from UniswapHandler.maltMarketPrice(), which derives the price directly from the Uniswap pool reserves. exitEarly() uses the calculated Malt quantity to mint Malt, sell it for collateral, and transfer the output to the exiting user. A flash loan can manipulate the reserves and therefore the spot price used for this early-exit settlement.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can manipulate the Uniswap spot price during an early exit and extract funds from the protocol.
ground_truth.mitigation: Use a TWAP oracle to track Malt's price instead of the current Uniswap reserve ratio.
ground_truth.title: [M-22] `_calculateMaltRequiredForExit` Uses Spot Price To Calculate Malt Quantity In `exitEarly`

ground_truth.description: StabilizerNode.stabilize() uses MaltDataLab's moving-average price to decide whether supply should be adjusted, but the supply-distribution path obtains the required minting trade size from UniswapHandler._calculateTradeSize(), which reads the current AMM reserves directly. A flash loan can temporarily distort those reserves before stabilize() is called, causing the protocol to mint and sell an excessive amount of Malt while distributing the received reward tokens.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can cause the protocol to remove most of the reward tokens from the AMM pool and distribute them as rewards, damaging the pool and destabilizing protocol accounting.
ground_truth.mitigation: Use a short TWAP or another manipulation-resistant price source to calculate the stabilization trade size instead of reading the current AMM reserves directly.
ground_truth.title: [M-25] AMM Pool Can Be Drained Using a Flash Loan and Calling `stabilize`

ground_truth.description: MaltDataLab derives Malt price and pool-reserve samples from current AMM reserves through trackMaltPrice(), trackPoolReserves(), and trackPool(), and writes those spot-derived observations into MovingAverage contracts. A well-funded actor can manipulate the AMM state around updater calls so that distorted observations are incorporated into the moving averages. Protocol operations that consume the resulting price or reserve averages can then act on manipulated economic data.
ground_truth.impact: Manipulated moving-average observations can cause auction, stabilization, collateral valuation, LP valuation, or reward-allocation operations to use incorrect economic data, enabling value extraction or protocol instability.
ground_truth.mitigation: Replace AMM spot-derived samples in MaltDataLab's moving averages with cumulative price observations, a TWAP implementation, or another manipulation-resistant oracle design so that updater calls cannot record attacker-controlled spot observations.
ground_truth.title: [M-30] Malt Protocol Uses Stale Results From `MaltDataLab` Which Can Be Abused By Users

predictions.description: MaltDataLab.trackReserveRatio() is publicly callable and writes a reserve ratio derived from live AMM reserves into reserveRatioMA without requiring UPDATER_ROLE. An attacker can temporarily manipulate the Malt/collateral pair, call trackReserveRatio() while the reserves are distorted, and then restore the pool. The contaminated moving-average value is later consumed by Auction.triggerAuction(), where it influences auction pricing and the pre-auction reserve ratio used during finalization.
predictions.impact: An attacker may influence auction starting and ending prices, auction economic terms, and the maximum burn budget used to purchase and burn Malt. This can cause excessive collateral deployment, incorrectly priced auctions, and value transfer to auction participants under manipulated conditions.
predictions.mitigation: Restrict trackReserveRatio() with onlyRole(UPDATER_ROLE), enforce a minimum observation interval, and feed the moving average from a manipulation-resistant TWAP or independently validated reserve-ratio source. Add deviation and range checks before accepting observations, and validate that auction reserve-ratio inputs remain within safe bounds before pricing or burn-budget calculations.
predictions.title: Permissionless reserve-ratio oracle updates enable auction manipulation

predictions.description: UniswapHandler.maltMarketPrice() derives Malt's price directly from current Uniswap V2 reserves. AuctionEscapeHatch._calculateMaltRequiredForExit() and earlyExitReturn() use this instantaneous price to calculate the amount of Malt to mint and sell for collateral. An attacker can temporarily skew the Malt/reward-token pool, invoke exitEarly() with a permissive minOut value, and cause the protocol to calculate an incorrect collateral payout using the manipulated price.
predictions.impact: The protocol may mint and sell an incorrect amount of Malt and transfer excessive collateral to an early-exit caller. The same manipulated price can also cause early-exit quote views to report inaccurate redemption values.
predictions.mitigation: Replace the spot reserve price with a sufficiently long TWAP, a validated MaltDataLab price, or an independent oracle with freshness and deviation checks. Enforce protocol-side price and output bounds, and do not rely solely on the user-controlled minOut parameter. Avoid using the same manipulable pool both as the pricing oracle and execution venue.
predictions.title: Spot AMM price controls auction escape-hatch collateral payouts

predictions.description: UniswapHandler._calculateTradeSize() calculates minting and burning trade sizes from instantaneous Uniswap reserves. These values are used by StabilizerNode._distributeSupply() and _startAuction() to determine how much Malt is minted or how much collateral is deployed to buy Malt. The reserve-derived amount is not checked against a TWAP or smoothed price. The resulting swaps in UniswapHandler.buyMalt() and sellMalt() also use amountOutMin equal to zero, allowing execution at any output amount after the manipulated sizing decision.
predictions.impact: An attacker may skew the AMM reserves before stabilization and cause the protocol to mint an excessive amount of Malt, deploy an inappropriate amount of collateral, create an oversized auction, or execute protocol-owned trades at an unfavorable price. This can cause excess issuance, collateral loss, price distortion, and reduced stabilization effectiveness.
predictions.mitigation: Use a manipulation-resistant TWAP or validated MaltDataLab price for trade sizing, and use the same protected oracle for stabilization authorization and operation sizing. Add maximum trade-size and per-call collateral limits, compare spot and TWAP prices, and pass meaningful minimum-output parameters to the router instead of zero. Revert when realized execution falls outside the permitted oracle-based range.
predictions.title: Spot reserves determine protocol stabilization trade sizes

predictions.description: UniswapHandler.getOptimalLiquidity() calculates the Malt amount required for a fixed reward-token amount using the current pair reserves. RewardReinvestor.provideReinvest() uses this result to call malt.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), maltLiquidity), without a user-supplied maximum Malt amount or minimum LP-token output. An attacker can manipulate the pair before the transaction is executed, causing the user to transfer an economically incorrect amount of Malt and add liquidity at a distorted ratio.
predictions.impact: Users may provide excessive Malt, receive less value than expected from reinvestment, or receive fewer or less valuable LP tokens. The transaction can also be exposed to sandwich-based value extraction by traders manipulating and then restoring the pool price.
predictions.mitigation: Use a TWAP or validated oracle-based quote instead of current reserves. Add user-controlled maxMaltInput and minLiquidityCreated parameters, enforce them during provideReinvest(), and pass explicit slippage limits to the liquidity router. Do not derive protection thresholds solely from balances calculated using the manipulated spot ratio.
predictions.title: Manipulable spot quote controls user Malt contribution during reinvestment

predictions.description: MaltDataLab.trackMaltPrice() reads instantaneous reserves from the configured Uniswap pair and submits the resulting spot price to maltPriceMA. Although the function is restricted to UPDATER_ROLE, the source does not show a delay, deviation check, or manipulation-resistant observation before an authorized updater records the value. MovingAverage stores the supplied value as lastValue for subsequent cumulative calculations. If reserves are manipulated when the updater records them, the contaminated sample can influence stabilization direction, auction pricing, and pool-transfer restrictions.
predictions.impact: A manipulated oracle sample may cause the protocol to incorrectly initiate an auction, distribute supply, calculate auction prices, or block transfers from the pool. The resulting protocol behavior can create unfavorable stabilization operations and financial losses depending on pool liquidity and updater timing.
predictions.mitigation: Feed maltPriceMA from a genuine time-weighted Uniswap observation or an independent validated oracle rather than an instantaneous reserve snapshot. Enforce minimum observation age, maximum deviation from the prior validated value, and sufficient sample history before allowing a new price to influence high-impact protocol actions. Keep UPDATER_ROLE tightly restricted and monitored.
predictions.title: Spot AMM reserves can be recorded into the Malt price oracle

ground_truth.description: VaderPoolV2.burn() redeems an LP position against the pool's current reserves and passes the released asset amounts together with the position's original deposits to VaderMath.calculateLoss(). Because the reserves can be manipulated before liquidity removal, an LP can create an artificial impermanent loss value. VaderRouterV2.removeLiquidity() then submits the resulting coveredLoss to the reserve for reimbursement.
ground_truth.impact: An LP can receive VADER compensation for artificially engineered impermanent loss. With a sufficiently large LP position, the reserve payout can exceed the manipulation costs and allow profitable extraction of reserve funds.
ground_truth.mitigation: Use a manipulation-resistant oracle, such as a TWAP, for the relative prices of the pool's assets when calculating impermanent loss.
ground_truth.title: [H-06] LPs of VaderPoolV2 can manipulate pool reserves to extract funds from the reserve.

ground_truth.description: LiquidityBasedTWAP.syncVaderPrice() rebuilds the VADER liquidity weights from zero and skips pairs whose update window has not elapsed. The skipped pair's previous weight is neither copied into pastLiquidityWeights nor added to the recomputed total, and a subsequent synchronization can therefore overwrite totalLiquidityWeight[Paths.VADER] with zero. _calculateVaderPrice() then uses the inconsistent weights and total when computing the VADER price, including division by the zero aggregate.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can cause VADER price calculations to use incomplete pair weights, making the oracle easier to manipulate, or force dependent price queries to revert. This can block protocol operations that call the VADER price, including USDV minting and reserve-funded impermanent-loss reimbursement.
ground_truth.mitigation: When a pair is not eligible for a TWAP update, preserve its previous liquidity evaluation in pastLiquidityWeights and include that value in _totalLiquidityWeight instead of leaving the pair weight at zero or resetting the aggregate.
ground_truth.title: [H-04] Vader TWAP weights can be corrupted and price queries can be forced to revert.

ground_truth.description: VaderPoolV2.mintSynth() reads the current native and foreign reserves and passes them to VaderMath.calculateSwap() to determine the synth amount. VaderPoolV2.burnSynth() reads the reserves again and uses the same reserve-based calculation to determine the native amount returned. Because the associated pool reserves can be moved before these operations, an attacker can mint synths at a manipulated exchange rate, restore or move the pool price, and redeem them at a more favorable rate.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can extract native-asset reserves from the associated VaderPoolV2 by manipulating the reserve-based exchange rate between synth minting and burning.
ground_truth.mitigation: Use a manipulation-resistant oracle for the exchange rates used by both synth minting and synth burning instead of relying on the pool's current reserves.
ground_truth.title: [H-07] Synth minting and redemption use manipulable pool reserves to drain native assets.

ground_truth.description: LiquidityBasedTWAP._updateUSDVPrice() calculates each USDV pair's currentLiquidityEvaluation by multiplying the pair's current native and foreign reserves by their configured asset prices. syncUSDVPrice() uses that value as the pair's liquidity weight, and _calculateUSDVPrice() weights the final oracle result with those values. An attacker can skew one underlying pool's reserves so its weight dominates the other pairs, causing the oracle to effectively price USDV/VADER from that pair alone.
ground_truth.impact: This reduces oracle resilience to a faulty or deprecated Chainlink feed. If the dominated pair's external feed is malfunctioning or deprecated, the manipulated weighting can cause the final oracle price to rely on that faulty feed and return an incorrect price; the finding does not establish direct fund loss by itself.
ground_truth.mitigation: Calculate fair reserves using the pool invariant and the fair prices of the two assets.
ground_truth.title: [M-06] Manipulated pool reserves can make the oracle rely on a single pair.

predictions.description: VaderPoolV2.mintSynth and burnSynth calculate synthetic conversion amounts directly from the current reserveNative and reserveForeign values using VaderMath.calculateSwap. These reserves can be changed by permissionless swaps through VaderRouterV2.swapExactTokensForTokens, which invokes BasePoolV2.swap and updates pairInfo reserves. Neither synthetic function uses a TWAP, external oracle, price-deviation bound, or user-supplied minimum-output parameter. An attacker can therefore move the pool price before a mint or redemption and cause synthetic assets to be issued or redeemed at a manipulated rate.
predictions.impact: Users may receive materially fewer synth tokens or native assets than expected, while favorable manipulation can cause excessive synth issuance or native-asset redemption. Repeated exploitation may create mispriced synthetic liabilities, deplete pool reserves, and transfer value between users, liquidity providers, and attackers.
predictions.mitigation: Price synth issuance and redemption using a sufficiently long and validated TWAP or an independent oracle rather than instantaneous reserves. Add user-controlled minimum-output parameters and deadlines, and reject execution when the pool price deviates beyond a configured threshold from the reference price. Review the reserve model so synth issuance and redemption cannot create inconsistent reserve-based pricing.
predictions.title: Spot reserve manipulation enables mispriced synthetic issuance and redemption

predictions.description: LiquidityBasedTWAP derives pair liquidity weights from current spot reserves during syncVaderPrice and syncUSDVPrice. The values are stored as pastLiquidityEvaluation and later determine each pair's contribution to the aggregate VADER or USDV price. Because synchronization is publicly callable and the underlying reserves can be changed through swaps, an attacker can distort a pair's reserve composition immediately before synchronization, record manipulated weights, and later influence the aggregate oracle price even after reversing the trade. The synchronization logic also replaces the global total with only pairs that updated during the call, temporarily excluding pairs whose update period has not elapsed.
predictions.impact: The aggregate oracle price used by USDV minting, USDV burning, and impermanent-loss reimbursement can be materially distorted. This may cause excess USDV issuance, excess VADER redemption or minting, and excessive reserve reimbursements. Incomplete pair inclusion can additionally produce unstable or malformed oracle outputs.
predictions.mitigation: Use time-weighted or otherwise historical liquidity measurements instead of spot reserves sampled at synchronization time. Recompute aggregate totals from all stored pair weights, retaining prior values for pairs that are not yet eligible for an update. Require nonzero totals, minimum pair liquidity, fresh observations, bounded per-update price changes, and independent reference-price deviation checks before accepting a new oracle value.
predictions.title: LiquidityBasedTWAP uses attacker-controlled spot reserves as historical weights

predictions.description: USDV.mint and USDV.burn consume prices returned by LiquidityBasedTWAP.getVaderPrice and getUSDVPrice. These prices are derived from cumulative prices of configured AMM pools and, for USDV pricing, VaderPoolV2 cumulative prices. An attacker can alter the underlying pool reserve ratio and maintain the manipulated state until the configured update period elapses, causing the LBT to record a distorted average price. The source permits any nonzero update period and does not enforce a minimum observation window, independent price validation, or maximum price deviation.
predictions.impact: A manipulated VADER price can cause USDV.mint to issue excess USDV for deposited VADER. A manipulated USDV price can cause USDV.burn to mint excess VADER for burned USDV, potentially diluting VADER holders and increasing protocol liabilities. The lock delay does not correct an incorrectly calculated conversion amount.
predictions.mitigation: Enforce a protocol-defined minimum TWAP update period and minimum liquidity threshold for configured pairs. Add independent oracle comparisons, maximum deviation and per-update movement limits, stale-data checks, and circuit breakers before accepting prices. USDV mint and burn operations should reject zero, stale, or abnormal prices and should support user-specified minimum-output protections.
predictions.title: AMM-derived LBT prices can manipulate USDV conversion rates

predictions.description: VaderRouterV2 transfers the nominal amountIn to BasePoolV2 and passes the same nominal value to swap or doubleSwap. BasePoolV2.swap does not measure the actual balance increase before calculating output or updating reserves. If a supported token charges transfer fees, rebases, or otherwise transfers fewer tokens than requested, the pool calculates output and records reserves as though the full nominal amount was received. BasePoolV2.doubleSwap performs a balance sufficiency check but still uses the nominal input rather than the actual transfer delta.
predictions.impact: The pool may pay output for tokens it did not receive and record overstated reserves. Subsequent swaps, liquidity withdrawals, cumulative prices, and oracle consumers can use corrupted reserve data, creating incorrect or manipulable prices and potentially causing direct pool losses or later transfer failures.
predictions.mitigation: Measure each token's actual balance increase relative to its stored reserve after the router transfer and use that value for swap calculations and reserve updates. Alternatively, explicitly reject any transfer where the received amount differs from the requested amount and restrict supported assets to standard ERC-20 tokens whose transfer behavior is compatible with nominal accounting. Apply the same validation to both legs of doubleSwap and update reserves from actual post-operation balances where practical.
predictions.title: Nominal swap inputs can corrupt price-bearing reserves for non-standard tokens

ground_truth.description: FlanBackstop.purchasePyroFlan() computes priceBefore and tiltedPrice directly from the instantaneous FLAN/stablecoin Uniswap pair balances. These values determine growth, flanToMint, and the premium ultimately minted to the caller as PyroFlan. An attacker can temporarily skew the pair balances with a flash loan or large trade and can split the operation into repeated smaller calls. The acceptableHighestPrice check only caps each observed tilted price and therefore does not make the spot inputs manipulation-resistant or stop a repeated attack within the configured limit.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can manipulate the FLAN/stablecoin LP, especially when it is new or has low liquidity, to receive large amounts of PyroFlan backed by newly minted FLAN. By reducing the volume of each flash-loan attack and repeating it, the attacker can accumulate this gain while remaining below the per-call price ceiling.
ground_truth.mitigation: Use a TWAP instead of the pool price at a single point in time to increase the cost of a flash-loan sandwich attack.
ground_truth.title: [H-05] Flash loan price manipulation in purchasePyroFlan()

ground_truth.description: LimboDAO.setEYEBasedAssetStake() and LimboDAO.burnAsset() calculate the EYE value of an EYE-based LP asset from the underlying EYE balance divided by the LP token total supply. Because the underlying pool balance is read at execution time, an attacker can temporarily manipulate the pool reserves before the LP asset is staked or burned and cause the protocol to use an inflated LP value.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can manipulate the underlying LP reserves to receive excess fate for an LP asset. The excess fate can provide disproportionate voting power and may be converted to Flan for direct profit.
ground_truth.mitigation: Use a fair pricing formula for LP tokens, such as a manipulation-resistant formula proposed by Alpha Finance.
ground_truth.title: [H-07] LP pricing formula is vulnerable to flashloan manipulation

predictions.description: FlanBackstop.purchasePyroFlan derives priceBefore and tiltedPrice from instantaneous Flan and stablecoin balances of the configured Flan/stablecoin LP. These balances can be influenced through swaps, temporary liquidity changes, or direct token transfers before execution. The resulting tiltedPrice determines flanToMint, while the difference between priceBefore and tiltedPrice determines the premium. The final amount is passed directly to PyroTokenLike(config.pyroFlan).mint(msg.sender, flanToMint + premium). The acceptableHighestPrice check only imposes an absolute upper bound on tiltedPrice; it does not validate either price against a historical, independent, or time-weighted reference and does not cap the premium.
predictions.impact: An attacker may cause the backstop to mint more PyroFlan than justified by the supplied stablecoin. Depending on the omitted PyroFlan redemption and market mechanics, this can dilute existing PyroFlan holders, increase redemption liabilities, consume protocol-controlled liquidity, and transfer value to the attacker. Manipulated downward prices can also cause purchases to revert because priceBefore - tiltedPrice underflows.
predictions.mitigation: Replace same-transaction balance-ratio pricing with a sufficiently delayed and manipulation-resistant reference, such as a Uniswap cumulative-price TWAP, an independently maintained oracle, or a medianized set of independent sources. Validate freshness and deviation from the reference, calculate issuance from the trusted price rather than tiltedPrice, and impose independent caps on total PyroFlan output and the premium. Also validate the actual stablecoin amounts received by each LP and explicitly handle priceBefore <= tiltedPrice and zero-balance cases.
predictions.title: Spot-price manipulation can inflate PyroFlan issuance

predictions.description: Limbo.setEYEBasedAssetStake and Limbo.burnAsset value approved LP assets using IERC20(domainConfig.eye).balanceOf(asset) divided by the LP total supply. The EYE balance of an LP contract can be increased independently of LP supply by transferring EYE directly to the LP. This changes eyePerUnit and therefore the implied EYE value used to validate staking and calculate Fate creation. In burnAsset, the same manipulated conversion directly determines fateCreated.
predictions.impact: An attacker holding an approved LP token may increase the LP's apparent EYE backing and obtain disproportionate Fate. Excess Fate can influence proposal creation and voting and may also be converted into Flan through convertFateToFlan, causing governance distortion and potential excess Flan issuance.
predictions.mitigation: Do not value LP tokens solely from the LP contract's raw EYE balance. Use canonical, synchronized reserves and account for unsolicited token donations, for example by valuing only recognized reserves or using the lower of recorded reserves and balances. Prefer a delayed or time-weighted valuation and add tests covering direct EYE donations, reserve synchronization, total-supply changes, and subsequent Fate creation.
predictions.title: LP EYE balance donations can inflate Fate valuation

predictions.description: UniswapHelper.stabilizeFlan calculates finalSCXBalanceOnLP and existingFlanOnLP from raw ERC20 balances held by the configured Flan/SCX pair. DesiredFinalFlanOnLP and the amount of Flan minted to the pair are then derived from these values and the stored Behodler quote. Direct token transfers or other balance changes can alter the apparent pair state without representing a validated market price or synchronized reserve state. The resulting LP position is minted to the black hole, so the protocol cannot recover the liquidity position.
predictions.impact: Manipulated pair balances can cause the helper to mint an unjustified amount of Flan into the external pair or mint too little during migration. This can dilute Flan, distort the intended Flan/SCX parity mechanism, and create incorrect migration liquidity outcomes. The two-snapshot Behodler quote controls reduce some quote manipulation risk but do not authenticate the external pair balances used by this function.
predictions.mitigation: Use canonical pair reserves and validate synchronization before calculating the target balance. Add independent and delayed price validation, maximum SCX and Flan balance-change limits, and a governance-controlled maximum Flan issuance per migration. Do not allow raw balance changes or unsolicited token donations to determine the mint amount.
predictions.title: Raw external-pair balances can cause excess Flan minting during stabilization

predictions.description: Limbo.claimSecondaryRewards transfers the entire Limbo balance of an eligible token to UniswapHelper.buyFlanAndBurn. The helper calculates amountOut from the current Flan and input-token balances of the configured pair using getAmountOut, then executes a swap and burns 99% of the received Flan while sending 1% to the caller. The calculation uses mutable spot balances and does not use a TWAP, independent oracle, minimum output, or caller-supplied slippage bound.
predictions.impact: An attacker can manipulate the relevant pair before the buyback and cause protocol-held tokens to be exchanged for less Flan than expected. This can reduce the amount of Flan acquired and burned, transfer value to an arbitrageur or caller, and permanently dispose of protocol assets at an unfavorable price. The operation is also susceptible to transaction-ordering and sandwich effects.
predictions.mitigation: Price the buyback using a sufficiently delayed TWAP or independent oracle and enforce a minimum acceptable amountOut based on that reference. Validate the expected pair and canonical reserves, add explicit slippage and maximum-loss controls, and consider batching or delaying buybacks to reduce transaction-ordering manipulation.
predictions.title: Spot AMM pricing can cause unfavorable protocol buybacks

ground_truth.description: NonUSTStrategy.investedAssets() converts the strategy's UST exposure into the vault's underlying asset using Curve's current get_dy_underlying() quote. Vault.totalUnderlying() includes that result, and deposit and withdrawal share calculations use totalUnderlyingMinusSponsored(). An attacker can temporarily move the Curve pool with a flash loan, make the same UST position appear to be worth more or less underlying, and deposit or withdraw while the vault uses that transient exchange rate.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can mint too many vault shares or withdraw more underlying than their fair share at the expense of existing depositors.
ground_truth.mitigation: Value the UST exposure with a manipulation-resistant oracle or sufficiently long TWAP instead of Curve's transaction-local quote.
ground_truth.title: [H-03] Vaults with non-UST underlying asset vulnerable to flash loan attack on curve pool

ground_truth.description: Vault.setStrategy() only permits replacing the current strategy when strategy.investedAssets() is zero. BaseStrategy.investedAssets() includes the raw aUST token balance held by the strategy, so anyone can transfer aUST directly to the strategy and make the zero-invested-assets check fail. The attacker can repeat this griefing after the protocol initiates and completes the required redemption flow.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can repeatedly prevent the protocol from replacing its strategy, delaying strategy maintenance or migration and forcing the protocol to process the outstanding aUST redemption flow before retrying.
ground_truth.mitigation: Track the strategy's internal aUST balance and update it on deposits and redemptions, then use that accounting instead of the raw aUST token balance when checking whether the strategy is empty. Alternatively, allow the strategy to transfer aUST back to the vault.
ground_truth.title: [M-11] Changing a strategy can be bricked

predictions.description: Vault.totalUnderlying() derives the vault asset value from underlying.balanceOf(address(this)), which includes arbitrary ERC-20 transfers made directly to the vault. These transfers do not mint shares or update depositor records. During deposit(), _createDeposit() calculates shares before receiving the new deposit, and _computeShares() divides the deposit amount by the inflated totalUnderlyingMinusSponsored() value. An attacker can make an initial deposit, transfer a sufficiently large donation directly to the vault, and cause a subsequent victim deposit to receive severely reduced or zero shares due to integer truncation. The victim's tokens are still transferred successfully by _transferAndCheckUnderlying(). Existing shareholders can then retain control over the vault assets, including the victim's deposit, while the victim may be unable to withdraw meaningful value.
predictions.impact: A nonzero deposit can result in zero or materially underpriced shares. The affected depositor may lose part or all of the deposited principal, while an attacker holding the existing shares may withdraw a disproportionate amount of vault assets. Direct donations also distort yield, withdrawal, and investment calculations.
predictions.mitigation: Use separately accounted assets for share pricing instead of treating every raw ERC-20 balance increase as distributable assets. Recognize deposits and other approved asset flows explicitly, and prevent unsolicited transfers from changing the exchange rate unless they are intentionally synchronized. Additionally, reject nonzero deposits that mint zero shares, support a user-supplied minimum share amount, use virtual assets and virtual shares where appropriate, and record the exact shares assigned to each deposit rather than recomputing withdrawal shares from a later exchange rate.
predictions.title: Share-price inflation through unsolicited underlying-token transfers

predictions.description: NonUSTStrategy uses the configured Curve pool's current get_dy_underlying() quote to value UST-denominated strategy assets in investedAssets(). This valuation flows into Vault.totalUnderlying(), share issuance, withdrawals, yield claims, and investment calculations. The same strategy executes conversions through exchange_underlying() with min_dy set to zero in both directions and ignores the returned output amount. If the configured Curve pool's spot state is moved before a strategy operation, the strategy can accept an unfavorable conversion price, while a manipulated quote can distort the vault's reported asset value and consequently alter share or withdrawal calculations. No TWAP, independent oracle, deviation bound, or minimum-output protection is present in the supplied source.
predictions.impact: The strategy may receive substantially fewer tokens than expected during underlying-to-UST or UST-to-underlying conversions. A distorted Curve quote can also cause incorrect asset valuation, excessive or insufficient share issuance, inaccurate yield claims, incorrect withdrawals, and incorrect amounts transferred to the strategy. Losses are borne by vault depositors and sponsors.
predictions.mitigation: Do not use a single instantaneous Curve quote as the sole vault valuation source. Use a manipulation-resistant oracle or sufficiently long-window TWAP, validate the result against an independent reference price, and reject stale or abnormal deviations. For both Curve swaps, calculate and enforce a nonzero minimum output based on a trusted price and configured slippage tolerance, and verify the actual received amount after execution.
predictions.title: Curve spot-price valuation and zero-slippage swaps in NonUSTStrategy

ground_truth.description: ERC4626Oracle.getPrice() values an ERC4626 vault share by calling previewRedeem() for a share amount and multiplying the returned assets by the oracle price of the underlying asset. previewRedeem() delegates to convertToAssets(), which derives the assets-per-share value from the vault's current totalAssets() and totalSupply. Because deposits, mints, withdrawals, and redemptions can change those spot accounting values within a transaction or block, an attacker can temporarily inflate or deflate the LP-token price returned by the oracle.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can make an ERC4626 LP token appear substantially more or less valuable than the underlying asset warrants. This can increase the attacker's borrowing power beyond the intended collateral value or make another account's collateral appear insufficient and trigger premature liquidation.
ground_truth.mitigation: Avoid using previewRedeem function to calculate the price of the LP token of an ERC4626 vault. Consider implementing TWAP so that the price cannot be inflated or deflated within a single block/transaction or   within a short period of time.
ground_truth.title: M-10: ERC4626Oracle Vulnerable To Price Manipulation

ground_truth.description: ERC4626.deposit() derives minted shares through previewDeposit() and convertToShares(), which rounds down assets multiplied by totalSupply and divided by totalAssets(). LToken.totalAssets() includes the underlying token balance held by the LToken, so an early depositor can mint a very small initial share balance and then transfer additional underlying assets directly to the LToken. This increases totalAssets() without increasing totalSupply, causing later deposits to receive an unfairly small number of shares.
ground_truth.impact: The attacker can capture value from future users' deposits. Later users can lose a material portion of their deposited assets when redeeming the shares minted at the manipulated price per share.
ground_truth.mitigation: Require a minimum amount of shares to be minted for the first minter.
ground_truth.title: H-1: LToken pricePerShare can be manipulated by an early depositor

predictions.description: UniV2LpOracle.getPrice() derives the LP-token price directly from the pair's current getReserves() values using a geometric-mean valuation. These reserves are instantaneous pool state and are not time-weighted, historically bounded, or checked against an independent valuation. Reserve-changing pair operations can therefore alter the value returned by the oracle before a consumer reads it. The supplied source does not include a downstream financial consumer, so the exact exploit transaction cannot be established; however, the attacker-influenceable reserve-to-price path is present in the oracle itself.
predictions.impact: If consumed for collateral valuation, borrowing, liquidation, minting, redemption, or settlement, an attacker may cause the protocol to use an inflated or understated LP-token value. This could enable excessive borrowing against LP collateral, incorrect liquidation decisions, or incorrect asset transfers and accounting.
predictions.mitigation: Replace the direct getReserves() dependency with a sufficiently long Uniswap V2 cumulative-price or other historical TWAP-based valuation, and require a minimum observation period. Add maximum-deviation and freshness checks against a stored or independently sourced reference price, validate that the pair is an approved canonical pair, and apply conservative collateral or valuation parameters in downstream consumers.
predictions.title: Uniswap V2 LP price relies on manipulable spot reserves

ground_truth.description: Balancer strategy vaults mint strategy tokens from a deposit using the pre-deposit BPT balance and global strategy-token supply, then convert strategy tokens back to BPT using the current total BPT balance and the unchanged global supply. A user can enter immediately before the permissionless reinvestReward operation adds reward BPT, so the user's newly minted strategy tokens participate in the reward distribution without any deposit-duration snapshot. The user can then redeem those tokens immediately and receive a disproportionate share of the newly reinvested BPT.
ground_truth.impact: Loss of assets for the users as their BPT gain (rewards) can be stolen.
ground_truth.mitigation: Use snapshot-based reward accounting so BPT gains are weighted by deposit duration, and prevent users from entering and exiting in the same transaction or block. As additional defenses, restrict reinvestReward to authorized Notional callers, charge fees to users who do not borrow from Notional, and submit reinvestment transactions privately to reduce front-running.
ground_truth.title: [M-7] Gain From Balancer Vaults Can Be Stolen

predictions.description: Boosted three-token vault valuation is described as time-weighted but is calculated from current Balancer pool balances obtained through getPoolTokens. The balances are passed into _getValidatedPoolData, used to calculate the StableMath invariant, and then used by _getTimeWeightedPrimaryBalance and _calcTokenOutGivenExactBptIn to determine the primary-token value of BPT and strategy tokens. An attacker can trade against the Balancer pool before a valuation or settlement operation and alter these balances, the invariant, and the resulting strategy-token valuation. The Chainlink spot-price checks constrain the accepted deviation but do not independently validate the final BPT-to-primary valuation or make the valuation time-weighted.
predictions.impact: Manipulated balances may cause strategy tokens to be overvalued or undervalued during convertStrategyToUnderlying and settlement. This could affect collateral valuation, liquidation behavior, settlement surplus checks, or cause settlement operations to revert when the calculated expectedUnderlyingRedeemed is inconsistent with the actual redemption value.
predictions.mitigation: Use a genuinely manipulation-resistant accounting valuation for boosted pools. Prefer a historical or time-weighted BPT-to-primary valuation, or independently derive and validate the final BPT price against Chainlink or another external oracle with a conservative deviation bound. Keep current pool balances only for execution-related calculations and do not use them as the sole basis for collateral or settlement valuation.
predictions.title: Boosted vault valuation relies on attacker-influenceable current pool balances

predictions.description: MetaStable strategy-token valuation directly uses the Balancer BPT_PRICE returned by getTimeWeightedAverage in _getTimeWeightedPrimaryBalance. This BPT price is not independently checked against Chainlink or another external valuation source. In addition, governance may configure balancerOracleWeight to 100%, allowing the pair-price component to be entirely Balancer-TWAP-based. Because Balancer TWAP values remain influenced by trades over the configured window, sustained pool manipulation can affect convertStrategyToUnderlying and settlement valuation.
predictions.impact: A manipulated Balancer oracle value may inflate or depress strategy-token valuations, affecting collateral values, liquidation thresholds, redemption expectations, and settlement accounting. An inflated valuation may cause settlement surplus checks to revert or permit inaccurate accounting, while a depressed valuation may cause premature liquidation or underpayment.
predictions.mitigation: Require a nonzero minimum Chainlink contribution for financially sensitive valuation and enforce a minimum, governance-bounded oracle window. Independently validate Balancer BPT_PRICE against a Chainlink-derived or otherwise independent BPT valuation, applying a conservative deviation limit before using it for collateral conversion or settlement. Do not permit a 100% Balancer-oracle configuration unless the BPT price is independently validated.
predictions.title: MetaStable strategy valuation can rely entirely on Balancer BPT TWAP

ground_truth.description: UniswapV3OracleWrapper.getOnchainPositionData() reads the pool's current price, but getTokenPrice() does not use that value. Instead, getTokenPrice() derives a square-root price from the protocol's token oracles and passes it to LiquidityAmounts.getAmountsForLiquidity(), then sums the resulting token amounts and pending fees at those oracle prices. The wrapper does not require a pool whitelist or a minimum TVL before valuing the position. An attacker can create a low-liquidity pool whose position is primarily theirs, deposit that position as collateral, borrow against the reported value, and swap the pool so the position's actual token composition no longer supports the collateral value.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can use a self-created low-TVL Uniswap V3 position as overvalued collateral, borrow from Paraspace, and then alter the position's pool composition so its realizable value falls below the outstanding debt, leaving the Lending Pool with a loss.
ground_truth.mitigation: Only allow Uniswap V3 positions from whitelisted pools that satisfy a sufficiently high TVL threshold before accepting them as collateral.
ground_truth.title: [H-05] Attacker can manipulate low TVL Uniswap V3 pool to borrow and swap to make Lending Pool in loss

ground_truth.description: When ParaSpaceOracle.getAssetPrice() has no nonzero primary-source price, it delegates to ParaSpaceFallbackOracle.getAssetPrice(), which derives the token price from the current WETH/token Uniswap V2 reserves and the router's getAmountOut(). Because these reserves are mutable spot state and the fallback does not use a manipulation-resistant oracle, a flash-loan attacker can move the pool price used for fallback valuation before a protocol operation reads it.
ground_truth.impact: If the primary oracle is unavailable, an attacker can manipulate the fallback spot price to overvalue collateral and borrow more than the collateral supports, or cause a malicious liquidation, leaving ParaSpace with bad debt.
ground_truth.mitigation: Do not use the Uniswap V2 spot price as a fallback when the primary oracle is unavailable; revert instead of returning a manipulable fallback price.
ground_truth.title: [M-04] Fallback oracle is using spot price in Uniswap liquidity pool, which is very vulnerable to flashloan price manipulation

ground_truth.description: NFTFloorOracle.setPrice() allows an administrator to finalize a price directly, while non-admin feeders pass through _checkValidity() and _combine(). For a newly added asset whose aggregated twap and updatedAt are zero, _checkValidity() accepts any positive first price and _combine() returns that feeder's value. A compromised feeder can front-run the administrator's enabling flow and submit an arbitrary initial price before the normal multi-feeder protections apply, making the newly accepted NFT appear overvalued.
ground_truth.impact: A compromised feeder can set an arbitrary initial NFT price, use the overvalued NFT as collateral, and borrow protocol funds, potentially draining protocol liquidity.
ground_truth.mitigation: Require an administrator to set a nonzero initial price before a new asset can be unpaused, or otherwise prevent an asset with a zero price from entering the feeder update flow.
ground_truth.title: [M-05] Front-running admin setPrice call allows a single compromised oracle to set any price, allowing the oracle manipulator to drain all protocol funds

ground_truth.description: NFTFloorOracle._checkValidity() compares a proposed twap only with the immediately prior aggregated twap and rejects a single update when its ratio reaches config.maxPriceDeviation. Because setPrice() can be called repeatedly and each accepted value becomes the next reference, individually permitted updates can compound within a short period; the oracle has no elapsed-time bound that limits the cumulative price movement.
ground_truth.impact: The configured maxPriceDeviation does not bound NFT floor-price movement over a short period, allowing the protocol to rely on a materially manipulated price despite the per-update deviation check.
ground_truth.mitigation: Use elapsed time and lastUpdated data to limit the maximum price change per oracle over a time interval, rather than only comparing consecutive updates.
ground_truth.title: [M-22] Price can deviate by much more than maxDeviationRate

predictions.description: The Dutch auction strategy derives the current auction price directly from block.timestamp: currentAuctionPrice = startPrice - (((startPrice - endPrice) * (block.timestamp - startTime)) / (endTime - startTime)). This value determines whether a taker bid is accepted through takerBid.price >= currentAuctionPrice. A block proposer or coordinated participant with limited ability to influence the block timestamp may advance the timestamp within consensus constraints, causing the calculated auction price to decrease and allowing a lower bid to execute earlier than it would under the intended wall-clock time. The maker's auction parameters are signature-protected, but the timestamp used in the calculation is not signed and is externally supplied by block production.
predictions.impact: A seller may receive a lower execution price than expected for the actual elapsed time, particularly in short-duration auctions or auctions with a large price decline. The impact is bounded by the underlying chain's timestamp constraints and does not provide arbitrary price control.
predictions.mitigation: Reduce reliance on fine-grained block timestamps for price progression. Consider using coarser price-update intervals, enforcing auction durations substantially larger than the expected timestamp deviation, and adding a signed seller-defined minimum execution price that is enforced independently of block.timestamp. If exact deterministic progression is required, consider a block-based or otherwise verifiable auction mechanism appropriate for the deployment chain.
predictions.title: Block Timestamp Manipulation Can Lower Dutch Auction Execution Price

predictions.description: ParaSpaceFallbackOracle.getAssetPrice derives ERC20 asset prices from the instantaneous reserves of a single Uniswap V2 WETH/asset pair using getReserves() and getAmountOut(). Uniswap V2 reserves are mutable through swaps, and the implementation does not use a TWAP, historical observations, minimum-liquidity requirement, deviation bound, freshness check, or independent reference price. ParaSpaceOracle.getAssetPrice invokes this fallback whenever the configured primary source is unset or returns zero, allowing an attacker-manipulated AMM price to flow into the protocol price oracle. The supplied pool interfaces indicate that oracle prices can influence collateral valuation, borrowing capacity, health factors, and liquidation decisions. Exploitability is conditional on the fallback being configured for an affected asset, the asset having a usable WETH pair, the primary source activating the fallback path, and the asset being used in financially sensitive protocol logic.
predictions.impact: An attacker may temporarily inflate or deflate the reported asset price by trading against the configured Uniswap V2 pair. If the manipulated price is consumed during borrowing or collateral assessment, the attacker could obtain excessive credit against overvalued collateral, avoid liquidation, trigger improper liquidations, or cause incorrect health-factor and collateral calculations. In the worst case, inflated valuations could create undercollateralized debt and protocol bad debt.
predictions.mitigation: Replace the instantaneous reserve quote with a manipulation-resistant source, preferably a trusted independent oracle or a sufficiently long Uniswap TWAP based on cumulative observations. If an AMM fallback is retained, require a minimum observation interval and liquidity threshold, validate freshness, compare the result against an independent reference price, enforce a maximum deviation, and restrict fallback support to explicitly approved assets and markets. Consider failing closed or pausing price-dependent operations when the primary oracle is unavailable rather than automatically accepting an unvalidated spot price.
predictions.title: Manipulable Uniswap V2 spot price used as fallback asset oracle

ground_truth.description: StakingModule.stakedByAt() reads an account's stake history through CheckpointsUpgradeable.getAtBlock(). When an account stakes and exits in the same block, the checkpoint history can contain both the large stake and the zeroed post-exit value for that block. The historical lookup can then return the earlier same-block stake value, causing balanceOfAt() to expose an incorrect historical balance even though the account no longer retains the corresponding stake.
ground_truth.impact: A same-block stake and exit can cause balanceOfAt() to report an incorrect historical stake. In this repository, the value is exposed through a standalone view and the slashing path uses the latest stake value instead. The direct consequence is inaccurate historical stake reporting; further loss requires a downstream integration that relies on this view.
ground_truth.mitigation: Require an account's exit to occur at least one block after the block in which the original stake was created, so a stake cannot be opened and closed within the same checkpoint block.
ground_truth.title: H-1: Flashloan `TEL` tokens to stake and exit in the same block can fake a huge amount of stake with minimal material cost

predictions.description: The non-TEL execution paths in FeeBuyback.submit transfer or forward the fee asset to the immutable aggregator and execute caller-supplied swapData using a low-level call. The contract only verifies that the aggregator call returned successfully and does not enforce a minimum TEL output, maximum execution price, price-impact bound, deadline, or post-swap TEL balance delta. If the underlying route uses attacker-influenceable liquidity, an attacker can manipulate the market or sandwich the owner-submitted transaction so that the swap executes at an unfavorable price. The resulting lower TEL amount is accepted and credited to the referral recipient. The direct TEL path does not perform a market swap and is not affected by this issue. Practical exploitability depends on the configured aggregator route and whether swapData independently contains effective slippage protection, which is not enforced by FeeBuyback.
predictions.impact: The safe's fee assets may be exchanged for substantially less TEL than intended, reducing referral rewards and potentially transferring value to arbitrageurs or sandwich attackers. Transactions can succeed despite economically unacceptable execution, and repeated unfavorable swaps may cause cumulative protocol losses. The contract also credits the entire TEL balance rather than only the balance increase from the current swap, which can further distort referral accounting.
predictions.mitigation: Add an explicit minTelOut and deadline parameter to submit. Record the TEL balance immediately before the aggregator call, execute the swap, calculate telReceived as the post-swap balance minus the pre-swap balance, and revert unless telReceived is at least minTelOut and the deadline has not expired. Credit only telReceived to the referral plugin. Where feasible, replace the unrestricted low-level call with a typed or dedicated aggregator adapter that validates the input token, input amount, TEL as the output token, the swap recipient, maximum input consumption, native value, and route-level slippage parameters. Aggregator calldata should also include a bounded minimum return and expiry as defense in depth.
predictions.title: Missing minimum-output protection on secondary buyback swaps

ground_truth.description: BLVaultLido allows an owner to deposit and withdraw around an external oracle update without a minimum holding period. On withdrawal it caps returned wstETH using only the current oracle price, while the Balancer exit executes against the pool state. An attacker can deposit while the pool matches the pre-update oracle, move the pool toward the known post-update price, wait for the oracle update, and then withdraw. Because the withdrawal check now uses the updated oracle, the vault returns the full manipulated wstETH amount instead of capturing the arbitrage for the Treasury.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can repeatedly sandwich predictable oracle updates to extract value from the vault, causing recurring losses to remaining vault liquidity.
ground_truth.mitigation: Lock the user into the vault for a minimum amount of time (i.e. 24 hours).
ground_truth.title: H-1: Adversary can sandwich oracle updates to exploit vault

ground_truth.description: CurveOracle.getPrice() retrieves the price of each underlying token in a Curve LP pool, selects the minimum price, and multiplies it by the LP token's virtual price to calculate its USD value. If the price of one or more underlying tokens is manipulated, the minimum-price calculation can be skewed and produce an incorrect USD value for the LP token. An attacker can exploit this incorrect valuation to profit at the expense of other users.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can manipulate the price used to value Curve LP tokens and profit at the expense of other users. Exploitation can result in significant financial losses for affected users.
ground_truth.mitigation: Use TWAP prices for the Curve pool's underlying assets.
ground_truth.title: H-4: Potential flash loan attack vulnerability in `getPrice` function of CurveOracle

predictions.description: The Curve, Convex, and Aura farming close paths perform financially sensitive conversions without meaningful minimum-output protection. CurveSpell.closePositionFarm() and ConvexSpell.closePositionFarm() call remove_liquidity_one_coin(..., 0), accepting any amount of debt tokens returned by the Curve pool. CurveSpell.closePositionFarm(), ConvexSpell.closePositionFarm(), and AuraSpell.closePositionFarm() also call swapExactTokensForTokens() with amountOutMin set to zero and an effectively unbounded deadline. AuraSpell additionally exits Balancer liquidity with a minAmountsOut array initialized entirely to zero. The ClosePosParam.sellSlippage parameter and ProtocolConfig.maxSlippageOfClose() are not applied in these paths. An attacker can influence the relevant Curve, Balancer, or router pool state before execution, causing the position assets or rewards to be exchanged at an unfavorable rate while the external calls still succeed.
predictions.impact: Position owners may receive materially fewer debt tokens from LP withdrawals and reward swaps, reducing refunds and repayment proceeds. Full closures may revert because the degraded proceeds are insufficient to repay the requested debt, leaving positions open and exposed to liquidation. Partial closures may succeed at an unfavorable rate and leave the owner with reduced value or residual debt.
