The transaction is atomic, so a failed close does not permanently consume collateral, but successful zero-minimum-output conversions can realize direct value loss.
predictions.mitigation: Add explicit user-supplied minimum outputs for every conversion leg. Pass a nonzero min_dy to Curve remove_liquidity_one_coin(), populate Balancer minAmountsOut with validated minimums, and pass per-swap amountOutMin values to reward-token swaps. Validate sellSlippage against bank.config().maxSlippageOfClose() and ensure it actually derives or constrains those minimums. Validate that each route starts with the expected input token and ends with the position debt token, restrict routers to approved implementations where appropriate, and replace type(uint256).max deadlines with caller-provided bounded deadlines. Expected outputs should be based on a trusted or manipulation-resistant quote and/or explicitly supplied by the user.
predictions.title: Close operations accept attacker-manipulated exchange rates

predictions.description: AuraSpell.openPositionFarm() joins a Balancer pool using a JoinPoolRequest with empty userData and no minimum BPT output enforcement. The function calculates poolAmountOut from current Balancer balances and total LP supply, but uses that value only to decide whether to call joinPool(); it is not passed as a minimum output or checked against the actual BPT balance increase. An attacker can alter the Balancer pool state before execution, causing the same borrowed assets to mint fewer BPT tokens while the spell continues and wraps the reduced LP balance as collateral.
predictions.impact: The user may receive less LP collateral for the borrowed assets, resulting in worse leverage and position economics. The operation may later fail its LTV or maximum-position checks, or it may succeed with reduced collateral and increased liquidation risk relative to the user's expectation.
predictions.mitigation: Encode the appropriate Balancer join kind and include a caller-specified minBptOut, or record the BPT balance before and after joinPool() and revert if the increase is below the required minimum. Derive the minimum from a user-approved slippage limit and a trusted or manipulation-resistant quote. Do not rely only on the later LTV or position-size checks, because those checks do not recover value lost during the join.
predictions.title: Balancer position entry lacks minimum BPT output protection

predictions.description: UniswapV2Oracle.getPrice() calculates LP-token value directly from the current reserves returned by pool.getReserves(). No TWAP, historical observation, independent deviation check, or other manipulation-resistance mechanism is applied to those reserves. The resulting LP price can flow through CoreOracle into BlueBerryBank.getPositionValue(), getPositionRisk(), isLiquidatable(), and the post-execution solvency check in execute(). It is also used by BasicSpell._validateMaxPosSize(). The exploitation path depends on the configured external Uniswap V2 pair allowing an attacker to influence the reserve values observed by the oracle; that external reserve-update behavior is not implemented in the supplied source, but the supplied code clearly trusts the mutable spot values for security-critical collateral decisions.
predictions.impact: If the configured pair state can be sufficiently distorted, LP collateral may be overvalued, allowing an undercollateralized position to pass borrowing or post-execution checks. After the manipulated state normalizes, the position may become liquidatable and the protocol may incur unrecovered debt. Liquidation and position-size calculations may also be temporarily incorrect.
predictions.mitigation: Replace reliance on current getReserves() values with a manipulation-resistant LP valuation. Use sufficiently long TWAP or historical observations, independently sourced underlying prices, conservative valuation haircuts, and configured deviation checks against an independent reference. Restrict routes to adequately liquid approved pairs, add reserve and liquidity sanity checks, and reject or pause valuation when the LP price changes beyond configured bounds.
predictions.title: Uniswap V2 LP valuation relies on mutable spot reserves

ground_truth.description: USSDRebalancer.getSupplyProportion() uses the raw USSD/DAI token balances held by a Uniswap V3 pool to calculate the rebalance amount. In Uniswap V3, those balances need not correspond to the current pool price because they include accumulated fees and can reflect liquidity placed in different price ranges. Consequently, when USSD is below peg, USSDamount can be lower than DAIamount and the subtraction in rebalance() can revert. When USSD is above peg, an attacker can use high-range single-sided DAI liquidity to inflate DAIamount, causing rebalance() to mint and sell more USSD than required to restore the peg.
ground_truth.impact: Rebalancing can malfunction when the USSD/DAI balance proportion is not as expected. An attacker can manipulate that proportion so the protocol mints and sells more USSD than required to restore the peg. If the collateral asset is also manipulated, the protocol can trade at a manipulated price, causing greater damage to the protocol.
ground_truth.mitigation: Replace the pool-balance-based rebalance delta with a formula that accounts for the Uniswap V3 liquidity range when calculating the amount required to restore the peg.
ground_truth.title: H-9: Uniswap v3 pool token balance proportion does not necessarily correspond to the price, and it is easy to manipulate.

ground_truth.description: USSDRebalancer.getOwnValuation() reads sqrtPriceX96 from the Uniswap V3 DAI-USSD pool's slot0() and derives the USSD valuation from the instantaneous pool price instead of a time-weighted average price. A user can temporarily move this spot price by buying or selling assets, including with flash-loaned funds, and then call rebalance() using the manipulated valuation.
ground_truth.impact: The USSD price used by rebalance() can be manipulated within a transaction, allowing an attacker to trigger rebalancing with an attacker-controlled valuation.
ground_truth.mitigation: Use a TWAP price instead of the instantaneous slot0 price when calculating the USSD valuation.
ground_truth.title: H-5: Price calculation susceptible to flashloan exploits

predictions.description: USSDRebalancer.getOwnValuation() reads the instantaneous Uniswap V3 pool price through uniPool.slot0() rather than a time-weighted or independently validated oracle. The publicly callable rebalance() function uses this value to select whether to sell collateral and buy USSD or mint USSD and sell it for collateral. An attacker can trade against the configured pool to move the spot price across the rebalance threshold, invoke rebalance(), and cause protocol-controlled assets to be traded based on the manipulated state. Rebalancing trade sizes are also influenced by current pool token balances, which can be changed through pool activity. The resulting swaps are executed by USSD.UniV3SwapInput() with amountOutMinimum set to zero, providing no execution-price protection.
predictions.impact: The protocol may mint USSD unnecessarily, sell collateral at an unfavorable price, buy USSD or collateral at manipulated rates, and transfer value to arbitrageurs. Repeated manipulation may cause incorrect or oscillating rebalancing and worsen the pool's imbalance. The maximum loss depends on pool liquidity, treasury balances, configured routes, and the cost of manipulating the pool.
predictions.mitigation: Replace the slot0() price with a sufficiently long Uniswap V3 TWAP or an independent oracle, preferably requiring agreement between multiple price sources and rejecting excessive deviations. Base both branch selection and trade sizing on the protected price. Add bounded minting and collateral-sale limits, cooldowns or sustained-deviation requirements, and meaningful amountOutMinimum values derived from a validated oracle price. A caller-supplied deadline should also be enforced for router execution.
predictions.title: Rebalancer relies on manipulable Uniswap V3 spot price

predictions.description: SimOracle.setPriceUSD() is publicly callable and directly changes the value returned by getPriceUSD(). If a SimOracle instance is configured for a mint-enabled production collateral, any caller can set an arbitrary price before calling USSD.mintForToken(). USSD.calculateMint() trusts the configured oracle result without independent validation and mints USSD to the supplied recipient based on that price. The same manipulated value is also used by collateralFactor() and by the rebalancer's collateral valuation logic. The production impact is conditional on SimOracle being registered as an active collateral oracle, but the attacker-controlled price-to-mint and price-to-accounting paths are present in the supplied source.
predictions.impact: An attacker can inflate the reported collateral price and mint more USSD than the deposited collateral is worth, potentially causing undercollateralization and losses to USSD holders or liquidity providers. Artificially low or high prices can also distort collateralFactor(), collateral selection, and rebalancing decisions. If SimOracle is restricted to isolated testing and never configured for production collateral, this finding does not affect the production deployment.
predictions.mitigation: Do not use SimOracle for production collateral. If it must be retained, restrict setPriceUSD() to a dedicated multisignature or governance-controlled role, require positive prices, emit price-update events, and enforce absolute and per-update deviation bounds. Maintain an allowlist of approved production oracle contracts in collateral configuration, validate freshness and oracle response validity, compare prices against an independent reference where possible, and impose mint caps or circuit breakers so a single abnormal price cannot create excessive USSD.
predictions.title: Permissionless SimOracle price updates can overvalue collateral and overmint USSD

ground_truth.description: EUSDMiningIncentives.stakedLBRLpValue() values a user's staked WETH/LBR LP tokens from the pair contract's current WETH and LBR token balances. During a Uniswap V2 flash-swap callback, the transferred-out assets temporarily reduce those balances before the swap is repaid. An attacker can therefore understate a victim's LP value, make isOtherEarningsClaimable() return true, and call purchaseOtherEarnings() while the eligibility check is using the manipulated value.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can redirect a victim's accumulated mining reward to themselves even though the victim has staked enough WETH/LBR LP tokens for the reward to remain protected from buyout.
ground_truth.mitigation: Use the WETH/LBR pair's recorded reserves returned by getReserves() instead of its live token balances when calculating the staked LP value.
ground_truth.title: [M-13] It is possible to manipulate WETH/LBR pair to claim reward of the users which shouldn't be claimed

ground_truth.description: Multipool.getSlots() reads each underlying Uniswap V3 pool's transaction-local slot0 price. _getReserves() feeds that price into LiquidityAmounts.getAmountsForLiquidity() to value the Multipool's positions, and deposit() uses the resulting reserves to optimize deposit amounts and calculate newly minted LP tokens. Because slot0 can be moved within a transaction, an attacker can distort the reserve ratio used for share issuance without changing the Multipool's durable economic value.
ground_truth.impact: A manipulated reserve calculation can cause deposits to mint an incorrect number of Multipool LP tokens, diluting other liquidity providers and causing them to receive fewer LP tokens or a smaller share of pool assets than intended.
ground_truth.mitigation: Use a manipulation-resistant TWAP or another independently validated price for reserve and share calculations instead of raw slot0. Reject deposits when each underlying pool's current price deviates beyond a configured bound from its weighted-average reference price.
ground_truth.title: H-3: Usage of `slot0` is extremely easy to manipulate

vulnerable_code.snippet: slots = getSlots(); (uint256 reserve0, uint256 reserve1, , ) = _getReserves(slots); ... lpAmount = l0 < l1 ? l0 : l1;
(uint256 amount0, uint256 amount1) = LiquidityAmounts.getAmountsForLiquidity(slots[i].currentSqrtRatioX96, ...); reserve0 += amount0; reserve1 += amount1;

predictions.description: Multipool._getReserves() values concentrated-liquidity positions using the instantaneous sqrtPriceX96 and tick obtained from each underlying Uniswap V3 pool through getSlots() and slot0(). These spot-derived reserves are used by Multipool.deposit() to optimize deposit ratios and calculate LP tokens minted, and by Multipool.snapshot() and Dispatcher deposit/withdraw flows to convert accrued token fees into LP-share withdrawals. The current tick also determines the branch used by _getFeeGrowthInside(), affecting pending-fee calculations. An attacker can temporarily manipulate an underlying pool price, cause a deposit or Dispatcher fee settlement during the manipulated state, and then restore the price, resulting in incorrect LP issuance, fee settlement, or share accounting.
predictions.impact: Users may receive too many or too few LP tokens, provide an unfavorable token composition, or have an incorrect number of tracked shares removed for fee claims. Value may be redistributed between the interacting user and existing LP holders. Reserve and claim estimates can also become materially incorrect during manipulation.
predictions.mitigation: Use a sufficiently long TWAP or another manipulation-resistant oracle for position valuation, pending-fee determination, deposit optimization, LP minting, and Dispatcher fee/share conversion. Alternatively, compare spot prices against validated TWAP prices and revert when deviation exceeds a protocol-defined bound. Prefer paying accrued token0 and token1 fees directly rather than converting them into LP shares using spot-derived reserve ratios. Add an explicit user-provided minimum LP-output or equivalent execution bound for deposits.
predictions.title: Spot-price manipulation affects reserve valuation and LP accounting

predictions.description: Multipool._initializeStrategy() reads each underlying pool's instantaneous slot0 tick and uses it in _getTicksForPosition() to determine the lower and upper ticks of every strategy position. The same unvalidated spot sqrt price is then used by _calcLiquidityAmountToDeposit() when opening liquidity. During the first owner deposit or an operator-authorized rebalance, an attacker can temporarily move an underlying pool price, causing the Multipool to establish ranges around the manipulated tick. Once the price returns, the positions may be out of range or have an unfavorable token composition.
predictions.impact: Existing LP holders may suffer reduced fee generation, misallocated liquidity, unfavorable asset exposure, and losses or additional costs when the strategy is later corrected. A rebalance can successfully execute while establishing liquidity at an attacker-influenced price.
predictions.mitigation: Derive position centers and ranges from a sufficiently long TWAP for each underlying strategy pool, or require the current spot tick and sqrt price to remain within a strict deviation from the corresponding TWAP before initialization. Apply the validation independently to every pool used by the strategy, and use validated pricing for both range selection and liquidity calculation. Add rebalance bounds for acceptable position centers and resulting token composition.
predictions.title: Strategy ranges are initialized from manipulable spot ticks

predictions.description: Multipool.getAmountOut() calculates the expected swap output from the arithmetic mean tick of the hard-coded fee-500 underlying pool over twapDuration. In rebalanceAll(), the execution is rejected only when actual output is below the oracle-derived output and the shortfall exceeds maxTwapDeviation. If an attacker manipulates the underlying pool sufficiently to make the TWAP quote artificially low for the swap direction, an unfavorable actual output can still satisfy amountOut >= swappedOut, causing the slippage check to be skipped. The rebalance is operator-restricted, but an attacker may manipulate or anticipate the underlying market during an operator-triggered rebalance.
predictions.impact: The Multipool may execute a materially unfavorable token swap while its TWAP protection accepts the transaction. The resulting loss reduces the assets backing LP tokens and is borne by Multipool LP holders. The practical impact depends on the underlying pool's liquidity, twapDuration, swap size, and whether the approved swap target applies independent minimum-output protection.
predictions.mitigation: Require an explicit operator-supplied minimum output and pass the same bound to the approved swap target. Treat the TWAP as an additional sanity check rather than the sole execution limit. Use conservative two-sided price bounds, a longer minimum TWAP duration, and preferably multiple validated pools or an independent oracle. Prevent twapDuration from being configured to zero or an excessively short interval.
predictions.title: One-sided TWAP validation can accept an unfavorable rebalance swap

ground_truth.description: MavEthOracle.getPriceInEth() reads the current token reserves of a Maverick boosted position, multiplies them by externally sourced token prices, and divides by boosted-position total supply. A flash-loan-funded swap can move the Maverick pool, alter getReserves(), and raise or lower the oracle LP-token value before reversing the swap.
ground_truth.impact: Decreasing the oracle price can lower the totalDebt of LMPVault and let a user receive more LMPVault shares. Increasing the oracle price can raise the totalDebt of LMPVault and let a user receive more withdrawn tokens. Manipulating the oracle price can also cause protocol miscalculations in the Stats contracts.
ground_truth.mitigation: Replace the transaction-local reserve-sum valuation with a Maverick-specific fair-LP calculation that derives fair reserves from trusted component prices and the position's applicable invariant.
ground_truth.title: H-15: Maverick oracle can be manipulated

predictions.description: UniswapV2EthOracle.getPriceInEth() values a registered pair using pair.totalSupply() and the current reserve0 and reserve1 returned by getReserves(). The reserve timestamp is ignored, and the implementation applies no TWAP, historical observation, reserve-change bound, liquidity threshold, or independent-price deviation check. Although the geometric-mean formula is generally appropriate for a 50/50 LP token and ordinary swaps primarily alter the reserve ratio rather than the reserve product, pair state remains externally changeable through liquidity operations, direct balance changes followed by synchronization, and other pair-specific behavior. If a registered pair is used as a vault underlying, or as a constituent dependency of a Balancer, Curve, or Maverick position oracle, the resulting price flows through RootPriceOracle into DestinationVault._debtValue() and can be persisted by LMPVault.updateDebtReporting() into totalDebt. The supplied source does not include deployment mappings proving that a live vault currently uses this configuration, nor does it demonstrate a guaranteed profitable extraction sequence; therefore, this finding is conditional on the relevant on-chain configuration and is assessed as Medium.
predictions.impact: A transiently distorted LP valuation may cause destination debt and LMP totalAssets/NAV to be overstated or understated. Subsequent ERC-4626 deposits, mints, withdrawals, redemptions, rebalances, and performance-fee calculations may use the incorrect cached valuation until a corrective debt report occurs. The same risk can propagate through composite Balancer, Curve, or Maverick valuation providers when their constituent-token mappings depend on this oracle.
predictions.mitigation: Replace instantaneous reserve-based valuation with a sufficiently long Uniswap V2 cumulative-price TWAP or an independently sourced LP valuation. Require a minimum observation interval, validate pair identity and liquidity, and reject or cap prices that deviate materially from prior observations or an independent reference. Before persisting debt reports, apply conservative deviation limits and consider using delayed or multi-observation prices. Review on-chain RootPriceOracle.tokenMappings and UniswapV2EthOracle.registrations to ensure that no financially sensitive vault asset depends on an unapproved spot-reserve source.
predictions.title: Uniswap V2 LP valuation relies on instantaneous reserve state

ground_truth.description: RdpxV2Core.bond() accepts a user-controlled bonding amount and, when reLP is active, passes that amount to ReLPContract.reLP(). The reLP operation then removes liquidity, swaps part of the removed WETH for rDPX, and adds liquidity again through Uniswap V2. Because the caller can control the size of this transaction-local liquidity operation through bond(), an attacker can manipulate the pool before bond() and profit from the resulting reLP sequence.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can steal value from RdpxV2Core by crafting a profitable sandwich attack around bond() and its indirectly triggered reLP operation.
ground_truth.mitigation: Remove ReLPContract.reLP() from bond() and trigger it separately to prevent users from controlling the reLP operation indirectly.
ground_truth.title: [M-08] `reLPContract.reLP()` is susceptible to sandwich attack due to user control over `bond()`

ground_truth.description: PerpetualAtlanticVaultLP.deposit() mints LP shares through convertToShares(). When the vault is empty, the initial deposit receives shares directly from the deposited assets, while later deposits calculate shares from totalSupply and totalVaultCollateral. Option settlement can add RDPX collateral to the vault and increase totalVaultCollateral without minting corresponding shares, so a malicious early depositor can make future deposits receive too few shares and then redeem an unfair portion of the vault assets.
ground_truth.impact: A malicious early depositor can profit from future deposits, causing later depositors to lose part of their deposited collateral.
ground_truth.mitigation: Require a non-trivial minimum initial share supply, for example by minting and permanently locking dead shares, so a small first deposit cannot disproportionately influence the share exchange rate.
ground_truth.title: [M-09] A malicious early depositor can manipulate the LP-Token price per share to take an unfair share of future user deposits

predictions.description: UniV3LiquidityAMO executes position minting, liquidity removal, and swaps against the mutable Uniswap V3 pool state. The contract forwards caller-supplied minimum amounts and price limits without validating them against a trusted oracle or TWAP. An attacker can temporarily trade against the public pool before an authorized administrator transaction. If the supplied minimums are zero, stale, or otherwise permissive, the AMO may mint liquidity, remove a position, or swap tokens at an economically unfavorable manipulated price. The fixed swap deadline of 2105300114 further allows old swap transactions to remain executable under materially different pool conditions.
predictions.impact: Protocol-owned rDPX and collateral can be exchanged at an unfavorable rate, liquidity can be minted with an unintended token composition, and positions can be fully removed at a manipulated price. The resulting value loss is borne by the AMO and RdpxV2Core reserves, while an attacker may profit by reversing the temporary pool manipulation.
predictions.mitigation: Validate all mint, removal, and swap parameters against a trusted, fresh oracle or sufficiently long Uniswap V3 TWAP. Enforce a maximum deviation from the reference price, require minimum output amounts consistent with that reference, validate sqrtPriceLimitX96, and use a short caller-supplied deadline bounded by the contract. Consider rejecting zero minimums for these operations.
predictions.title: Uniswap V3 AMO operations lack enforced manipulation-resistant price bounds

predictions.description: ReLPContract.reLP() reads instantaneous Uniswap V2 reserves and uses them in the liquidity removal and re-LP workflow. The operation subsequently swaps token B for token A against the same AMM and adds liquidity with both minimum amounts set to zero. When reLP is triggered from the public bond() or bondWithDelegate() flow while isReLPActive is enabled, an attacker can temporarily manipulate the pair before the transaction executes. The reserve-dependent sizing term is partially offset by the subsequent LP calculation, but the swap and final addLiquidity() remain exposed to the manipulated pool state, and no oracle/TWAP deviation or post-operation value check is enforced.
predictions.impact: The protocol may remove and recreate liquidity using an unfavorable token ratio, receive less economically valuable exposure than intended, or repeatedly revert when manipulation causes the intermediate minimum checks to fail. This can reduce protocol-owned LP value or disrupt public bonding operations.
predictions.mitigation: Use a manipulation-resistant TWAP or independently governed oracle for reserve valuation and re-LP sizing. Reject execution when the AMM price deviates beyond a bounded threshold, calculate nonzero minimum amounts for the final addLiquidity() call, and enforce an expected minimum LP output or post-operation value conservation check. Consider separating reLP from the public bonding path and executing it through a controlled keeper operation with fresh execution bounds.
predictions.title: ReLP relies on manipulable V2 reserves and performs unbounded final liquidity addition

ground_truth.description: MagicLpAggregator.latestAnswer() calculates the MagicLP token price from pool reserves. Because those reserve values can be manipulated, an attacker can use a flash loan to inflate the MagicLP oracle price.
ground_truth.impact: A flash-loan-funded swap can substantially inflate the MagicLP oracle valuation within one transaction.
ground_truth.mitigation: Before using pool reserves, compare the pool's base/quote price with the Chainlink-derived base/quote price and revert when the deviation exceeds a defined limit.
ground_truth.title: [H-04] Oracle price can be manipulated

ground_truth.description: Because _twapUpdate() runs after the reserves change, an attacker can make the TWAP accumulator attribute the entire elapsed interval to the manipulated post-update price. An integrating application that later reads the TWAP may therefore receive an attacker-controlled price.
ground_truth.impact: Applications that use MagicLP's TWAP to determine token prices can execute trades or other price-dependent operations at an attacker-controlled price, allowing value to be extracted from the integrating application.
ground_truth.mitigation: Call _twapUpdate() before updating the reserves.
ground_truth.title: [H-01] Anyone making use of the MagicLP's TWAP to determine token prices will be exploitable.

ground_truth.description: V3Oracle.getValue() computes position token amounts from the current Uniswap V3 slot0() price and values them using oracle-derived token prices. _checkPoolPrice() bounds the current pool price against the oracle-implied pool price through maxPoolPriceDifference, but an overly permissive setting can still materially distort the valuation of tight-range positions.
ground_truth.impact: With a tight-range position and a fringe or incorrect maxPoolPriceDifference configuration, an attacker can cause non-dust collateral misvaluation and borrow against an overstated position value. The check limits the effect for wide-range positions and properly constrained configurations; repay() is unaffected because it does not use the oracle.
ground_truth.mitigation: Calculate amount0 and amount1 from the oracle-derived price rather than the current pool spot price returned by slot0().
ground_truth.title: [M-19] `V3Oracle` susceptible to price manipulation

predictions.description: V3Oracle.setTokenConfig() accepts twapSeconds == 0 for all non-reference token modes, including Mode.TWAP, Mode.CHAINLINK_TWAP_VERIFY, and Mode.TWAP_CHAINLINK_VERIFY. When the configured period is zero, _getReferencePoolPriceX96() reads the current Uniswap V3 pool slot0() price instead of a historical observation. The resulting spot-derived price is used by V3Oracle.getValue() to calculate the LP position value, which V3Vault._checkLoanIsHealthy() uses to determine collateralValue and loan health. This directly affects V3Vault.borrow(), where a passing health check results in transfer of the vault asset to the borrower, and V3Vault.liquidate(), where the same values determine liquidation eligibility and liquidation economics. The final _checkPoolPrice() comparison does not provide independent protection because it also reads the position pool's current spot price with a zero-second period. The issue is conditional on deployment or governance selecting a TWAP-dependent mode with twapSeconds == 0, but the source does not prevent that unsafe configuration.
predictions.impact: An attacker who can manipulate the configured reference pool, and where necessary the collateral position pool consistently, may cause collateral to be overvalued and borrow more vault assets than the position supports. After prices normalize, the vault may hold undercollateralized debt and incur losses shared by reserves or lenders. Manipulated values can also make loans appear healthy, delay liquidation, or distort liquidationValue, liquidatorCost, reserveCost, and the collateral transferred to liquidators.
predictions.mitigation: Reject zero and insufficiently short TWAP periods for every mode that uses TWAP pricing. Enforce a protocol-level minimum such as MIN_ORACLE_TWAP_SECONDS and validate the existing stored period in setOracleMode() before allowing a token to enter a TWAP-dependent mode. Prefer Chainlink-backed pricing with an independently sourced, sufficiently long Uniswap TWAP as verification. Do not use the current slot0() price as the sole collateral price source, and avoid using the same manipulable spot state for both valuation and consistency validation. Existing deployments should be reviewed for TWAP-dependent configurations with twapSeconds == 0.
predictions.title: Zero-second TWAP configuration enables spot-price manipulation of collateral valuation

predictions.description: V3Oracle._initializeState() obtains the collateral position pool's current sqrtPriceX96 and tick from pool.slot0(). V3Oracle._getAmounts() then passes that spot-derived price to LiquidityAmounts.getAmountsForLiquidity() to calculate the position's amount0 and amount1. V3Oracle.getValue() prices those spot-dependent token amounts and returns fullValue and feeValue to V3Vault._checkLoanIsHealthy(). Consequently, even when the token price source is Chainlink or a nonzero TWAP, a temporary manipulation of the position pool spot can change the token composition used in collateral valuation. The oracle's consistency check compares the derived price against the same position pool's current spot price and accepts deviations below the configured maxPoolPriceDifference, so it is not an independent historical validation of the spot-derived composition.
predictions.impact: A sufficiently economical spot manipulation can alter the reported value of an LP position and therefore affect borrowing eligibility, maximum borrowable debt, liquidation eligibility, and the amount of collateral allocated during liquidation. A resulting overvaluation may permit additional borrowing and create bad debt after the pool returns to its normal price. The magnitude depends on the position range, pool liquidity, configured deviation threshold, collateral factors, and deployment configuration.
predictions.mitigation: Calculate LP token amounts using a sufficiently long, validated TWAP tick rather than the instantaneous slot0() price, or apply a conservative valuation that cannot overstate collateral during temporary spot movements. Use an independent oracle or historical observation for the position-pool consistency check instead of passing zero to _getReferencePoolPriceX96(). Consider blocking new borrowing when spot and TWAP composition or price differ beyond a conservative threshold, while retaining a separate robust path for liquidation.
predictions.title: LP collateral composition is calculated from manipulable spot price

ground_truth.description: WooPPV2 enforces maxNotionalSwap and maxGamma independently for each swap, then writes the swap's newPrice back to WooracleV2_2. A later swap in the same transaction reads that already-moved price as its starting state. Consequently, an attacker can split a flash-loaned WOO sale into multiple individually permitted swaps, compound the WOO price downward, and then sell a small amount of quote token at the manipulated price to receive more WOO than was borrowed. For a token without a configured Chainlink reference, WooracleV2_2 treats the nonzero internal price as in-bound, so the feasibility check does not provide an independent anchor.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can extract the pool's base-token reserves and repay the flash loan from the proceeds, retaining the excess tokens as profit.
ground_truth.mitigation: Explicitly declare that tokens without a Chainlink price feed are not supported.
ground_truth.title: H-1: Pool can be drained

predictions.description: WooCrossFee.currentBalance() reads the numeric price returned by wooracle.price(base) but discards the accompanying feasibility flag. WooracleV2.price() can return a nonzero Wooracle price with feasible == false when the posted price is outside the configured Chainlink deviation bound. The supplied WooPPV2 implementation updates Wooracle prices during public swaps through postPrice(), allowing a permitted swap to alter the price subsequently used by WooCrossFee. The manipulated valuation is then consumed by ingressFee() and outgressFee(), which are used by WooUsdOFTCrossRouter to determine bridge amounts and fee accounting.
predictions.impact: An attacker may influence cross-chain ingress or egress fees by moving the WooPPV2-derived oracle price before fee calculation. This can cause users to be overcharged or undercharged, move fees across configured fee-curve thresholds, reduce protocol fee revenue, and alter the net amount bridged or swapped.
predictions.mitigation: Require feasible == true for every price used by WooCrossFee.currentBalance(), or use a separately validated fallback such as a fresh Chainlink price. Reject zero, stale, negative, or out-of-bound oracle values. For stronger protection, use a TWAP or independent valuation source for fee accounting and apply bounds to changes in the calculated balance and resulting fee.
predictions.title: Infeasible Wooracle prices influence cross-chain fee calculations

predictions.description: WooRebateManager.claimRebate() and WooVaultManager.distributeAllReward() execute quote-token to reward-token conversions through WooRouterV2.swap() with minToAmount set to zero. Where the configured router uses WooPPV2, public swaps can update the Wooracle price through WooPPV2.postPrice(), and the subsequent reward conversion may execute at a price influenced by recent trading activity. The displayed rebate quote from pendingRebateInReward() is not enforced during claim execution, and the full vault reward balance is converted without a protocol-defined minimum output.
predictions.impact: A rebate claimant may receive materially fewer reward tokens than expected, and vault users may receive reduced distributions when the full reward balance is converted at an unfavorable manipulated spot price. Large conversions may be economically attractive to sandwich or otherwise influence, subject to WooPP limits, liquidity, oracle configuration, and deployment wiring.
predictions.mitigation: Add a caller- or keeper-supplied minimum-output parameter and pass it to WooRouterV2.swap(). For rebate claims, require the obtained reward amount to satisfy the user's minimum. For vault distributions, derive a conservative minimum from an independent, fresh oracle or TWAP, split large conversions into bounded transactions, and reject execution when the relevant oracle price is stale or infeasible.
predictions.title: Reward conversions execute without minimum-output protection

ground_truth.description: PanopticFactory._mintFullRange() reads the Uniswap V3 pool's instantaneous sqrt price from slot0() and uses it to calculate the full-range liquidity minted during deployNewPool(). Because the factory does not validate this price against an oracle or a time-weighted average, an attacker can manipulate the spot price with flash-loaned funds before deployment and cause a highly inaccurate liquidity calculation.
ground_truth.impact: The manipulated spot price can cause the factory to mint an inaccurate amount of liquidity for each token, resulting in an unbalanced newly deployed pool.
ground_truth.mitigation: Consider using the TWAP price instead of the spot price.
ground_truth.title: [M-01] `PanopticFactory` uses spot price when deploying new pools, resulting in liquidity manipulation when minting

predictions.description: PanopticMath.twapFilter() computes 19 interval tick measurements, sorts them, and returns sortedTicks[10]. For 19 zero-indexed values, the median is sortedTicks[9]; sortedTicks[10] is the upper adjacent order statistic. This introduces an upward bias and allows nine manipulated high samples to influence the returned value in scenarios where ten would be required to move the true median. The resulting tick is used by PanopticPool for forced-exercise eligibility, exercise-fee calculations, liquidation valuation, and other price-sensitive decisions.
predictions.impact: An attacker who can influence enough Uniswap observation intervals may obtain an attacker-favorable oracle tick. This can affect forced-exercise authorization, exercise compensation, liquidation eligibility, collateral valuation, and liquidation bonus calculations. The exact economic impact depends on the underlying pool liquidity and position parameters.
predictions.mitigation: Return the actual median element, sortedTicks[9], or derive the index from an explicit measurement-count constant such as NUM_MEASUREMENTS / 2. Add tests covering the number of manipulated intervals required to move the returned oracle value and validate that the intended order statistic is used.
predictions.title: TWAP filter returns the upper adjacent order statistic

predictions.description: PanopticPool._validateSolvency() always checks solvency at fastOracleTick but checks slowOracleTick only when the absolute difference between the two exceeds MAX_SLOW_FAST_DELTA. The fast oracle is derived from only three recent observation intervals. An attacker who influences the fast oracle while keeping its difference from the slow oracle at or below 1,800 ticks can cause the account to be evaluated only at the favorable fast price. The selected tick directly affects collateral requirements, token conversion, and the final solvency decision.
predictions.impact: An undercollateralized account may pass minting, burning, premium settlement, or forced-exercise-related solvency checks at a favorable manipulated fast price. This can increase protocol exposure and may result in losses when the account later becomes insolvent.
predictions.mitigation: Require solvency at both fastOracleTick and slowOracleTick for security-sensitive operations, or calculate both outcomes and reject the operation if either fails. If only one result is used for gas reasons, select the more conservative account-specific result rather than relying solely on the numerical difference between oracle ticks. Consider strengthening the fast oracle observation horizon and adding an appropriate current-price consistency bound.
predictions.title: Solvency validation can rely solely on the short-window fast oracle

predictions.description: PanopticPool.forceExercise() determines exercisability using the historical twapTick but separately reads the current Uniswap spot tick from slot0().tick. It does not require the two values to be close and does not require the position to be exercisable at the current tick. The spot tick is then passed to CollateralTracker.exerciseCost(), where it controls the distance from the strike and the exponentially decaying force-exercise fee. The TWAP is also used for refund conversion. An attacker can move the spot price before forceExercise while leaving the TWAP substantially unchanged, or exploit a stale TWAP after the spot has moved, thereby affecting forced-exercise authorization and settlement.
predictions.impact: A position may be forcibly closed while it is no longer out-of-range at the current AMM price. In addition, a manipulated spot tick can reduce or otherwise distort the exercise compensation paid to the exercisee and alter token0/token1 refund composition. The resulting value transfer can disadvantage the forced-exercisee or create an unfair benefit for the exercisor.
predictions.mitigation: Add an explicit widened-int256 currentTick-versus-twapTick deviation check in forceExercise(), using a threshold appropriate for forced exercise. Additionally, require exercisability at both the oracle and current prices if current out-of-range status is required. Prefer using one validated manipulation-resistant oracle tick consistently for exercisability, strike-distance fee calculation, and refund conversion; alternatively, clamp any spot tick used for settlement to a permitted range around the oracle.
predictions.title: Forced exercise uses inconsistent and manipulable spot/TWAP prices

predictions.description: Premium calculations in PanopticPool use the current Uniswap spot tick as the atTick argument. The value is forwarded through _calculateAccumulatedPremia() and _getPremia() to SemiFungiblePositionManager.getAccountPremium(), which invokes FeesCalc.calculateAMMSwapFees(). The fee-growth calculation branches depending on whether the supplied tick is below, within, or above the liquidity range. The resulting premium affects margin balances, collateral requirements, liquidation eligibility, forced-exercise delegation, and settled-token accumulators. The settleLongPremium() path likewise reads slot0().tick and commits the resulting premium to storage.
predictions.impact: A temporary spot-price movement across a liquidity-range boundary can alter pending premium calculations. Depending on the operation, this may cause incorrect solvency outcomes, incorrect liquidation accounting, incorrect forced-exercise funding, or an incorrect amount of premium to be credited to sellers. The liquidation spot/TWAP bound limits one path but does not make the premium calculation oracle-based and does not protect the other premium-sensitive operations.
predictions.mitigation: Use a validated manipulation-resistant oracle tick for premium calculations whenever the result affects solvency, liquidation, forced exercise, or settlement. If current spot state is required for exact fee-growth accounting, apply a consistent spot/TWAP deviation bound before using the result in financial decisions and add regression tests for ticks below, inside, and above the relevant liquidity range.
predictions.title: Spot tick influences pending premium accounting in security-sensitive paths

ground_truth.description: PanopticPool.pokeOracle() is permissionless and passes the current Uniswap pool tick to RiskEngine.computeInternalMedian(). OraclePack.computeInternalMedian() records the observation only when the current epoch differs from the recorded epoch. An attacker can manipulate the pool's current tick before an update, cause that value to be clamped and inserted into the internal oracle, and prevent later calls in the same epoch from replacing it. Repeating this across epochs can progressively move the oracle away from the legitimate market price.
ground_truth.impact: Manipulating the internal oracle causes positions to be evaluated at incorrect prices, which can produce incorrect solvency validations, unfair liquidations, or allow insolvent positions to remain active.
ground_truth.mitigation: Update the oracle continuously with the current tick as time progresses, similar to a Uniswap TWAP, instead of allowing only one update per epoch. Alternatively, restrict pokeOracle() to trusted callers or use a commit-reveal scheme to prevent frontrunning.
ground_truth.title: [M-11] An attacker can manipulate oracle easily

ground_truth.description: RiskEngine.twapEMA() destructures OraclePack.getEMAs() in the wrong order: it treats the returned (spotEMA, fastEMA, slowEMA, eonsEMA, medianTick) tuple as (eonsEMA, slowEMA, fastEMA, ...). The intended weighted TWAP therefore uses the wrong EMA values, includes the spot EMA in place of the eons EMA, and omits the eons EMA. PanopticPool.getTWAP() uses this value in liquidation and force-exercise checks, so rapid adverse price movements can leave the TWAP near a stale value and cause an unhealthy account to appear solvent at that check.
ground_truth.impact: Unhealthy accounts can appear solvent at that tick and block liquidation/force-exercise (`NotMarginCalled`), delaying cleanup and risking larger bad debt or mispriced exercises/settlements.
ground_truth.mitigation: Destructure the EMAs in the correct order so the intended fast/slow/eons weighting is applied, and add a regression test proving that twapEMA uses those three EMAs rather than the spot EMA.
ground_truth.title: [M-03] TWAP misweights EMAs in RiskEngine, anchoring liquidation price to slow EMA and letting insolvent accounts dodge liquidation

ground_truth.description: When riskParameters.feeRecipient() is zero, CollateralTracker.settleMint() and settleBurn() burn shares from the option owner without removing the corresponding assets. This decreases totalSupply while leaving totalAssets approximately unchanged, immediately increasing the share value for holders at that moment. RiskEngine maps builderCode == 0 to address(0), and PanopticPool's liquidation and force-exercise paths request getRiskParameters(0), so a searcher can deposit before a commission-burn event and exit after it to capture value intended for incumbent liquidity providers.
ground_truth.impact: Just-In-Time entrants can capture commission distributions intended for longer-term liquidity providers. A sufficiently dominant entrant can also reduce the effective commission through fee self-rebating, weakening the fee model and LP incentives.
ground_truth.mitigation: Avoid instantaneous burn-based commission distribution. Treat builderCode == 0 as a non-zero protocol or treasury recipient, or distribute commissions through a time-weighted or streamed mechanism; any cooldown must also account for transfers so it cannot be bypassed.
ground_truth.title: [M-15] Commission share-burn distribution is JIT-capturable when `builderCode == 0` (default)

predictions.description: Several financially sensitive PanopticPool paths obtain the live Uniswap tick through getCurrentTick() and pass it into premium calculations. In particular, getAccumulatedFeesAndPositionsData() and _validateSolvency() use the raw current tick when calling _calculateAccumulatedPremia(), which forwards it to SFPM.getAccountPremium(). For Uniswap V3, FeesCalc.calculateAMMSwapFees() uses the supplied tick to select the fee-growth-inside branch based on whether the tick is below, above, or within the position range. An attacker who temporarily moves the underlying AMM price can therefore influence premium attribution and the premium values subsequently used in collateral and solvency calculations. The current-tick/TWAP consistency check is applied in dispatchFrom(), but it is not a universal check for all raw-tick consumers, including premium valuation and settlement paths.
predictions.impact: A temporary AMM price displacement may cause incorrect premium accounting and distort collateral or solvency results. Depending on active positions and liquidity, this could enable favorable premium settlement, premature or delayed liquidation behavior, or protocol and liquidity-provider losses.
predictions.mitigation: Separate execution pricing from valuation pricing. Use a protocol-approved EMA, median, or historical TWAP for premium, collateral, solvency, settlement, and payout calculations, or require every raw current-tick consumer to validate the live tick against an independently calculated oracle value using an operation-specific deviation bound. For AMM operations, validate the price before and after execution while using the validated oracle price for accounting. Consider reverting premium and collateral-affecting operations when the current tick is materially inconsistent with the oracle.
predictions.title: Raw AMM tick influences premium and solvency accounting

predictions.description: PanopticPool.pokeOracle() is permissionless and advances the internal OraclePack using the current Uniswap AMM tick. OraclePackLibrary.computeInternalMedian() accepts a new observation once the 64-second epoch changes, and clampTick() only limits the observation relative to the previous stored observation by MAX_CLAMP_DELTA. The observation remains derived from the instantaneous, attacker-influenceable AMM price rather than a historical TWAP or independently verified reference. An attacker who maintains an artificial AMM price can call pokeOracle() across successive epochs, gradually replacing entries in the eight-observation median queue and moving the spot, fast, slow, and eons EMAs. The resulting oracle state is consumed by getTWAP(), getSolvencyTicks(), liquidation bonus calculations, forced-exercise pricing, and collateral conversion.
predictions.impact: Sustained AMM manipulation can bias the internal median and EMA oracle, potentially causing solvent accounts to appear insolvent, allowing undercollateralized accounts to pass risk checks, or altering liquidation bonuses, forced-exercise compensation, and cross-token collateral conversions. The clamp and epoch gating limit the speed of manipulation but do not eliminate the cumulative poisoning path.
predictions.mitigation: Source accepted oracle observations from a historical Uniswap observation-based TWAP or median window covering a meaningful portion of each epoch instead of directly using slot0/currentTick. Add an independent reference-price or cumulative-deviation check, require a minimum observation interval based on actual elapsed time, and consider requiring agreement between the internal oracle and an independent historical price before liquidation, forced exercise, or other value-transferring operations. Retain the per-update clamp and multi-tick checks as supplementary controls.
predictions.title: Permissionless spot-fed oracle can be gradually poisoned
